title: Comparative Analysis of Automated Red Teaming in LLMs: AttnGCG, GPTFuzzer, and PAPILLON
abstract: Automated red-teaming methods enable systematic adversarial testing of Large Language Models, yet direct comparisons across different attack paradigms remain scarce, particularly regarding the trade-off between attack effectiveness and operational cost. We present a controlled comparison of three frameworks spanning distinct strategies: (i) AttnGCG; (ii) GPTFuzzer; and (iii) PAPILLON. All three are evaluated against Llama 3.1 8B Instruct on 18 adversarial goals drawn from HarmBench, using LlamaGuard-3 as a unified judge and an equal budget of 500 iterations per goal. Our results suggest seed-pool-based mutation offers the most favorable cost-effectiveness ratio against the evaluated target model, while gradient-based suffix optimization alone proves largely ineffective against recent safety-aligned architectures within practical iteration budgets. Although PAPILLON is designed to overcome the dependence on pre-existing templates, this advantage comes at a significantly higher operational cost compared to GPTFuzzer, since each mutation is tailored to a specific goal rather than shared across all goals simultaneously.

title: A Related Line of Research RegTutor: Self-correcting Agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Medical-Device Compliance Training
abstract: Medical-device compliance training requires feedback grounded in authoritative regulations. However, existing retrieval-augmented generation approaches often lack explicit evidence assessment and post-generation validation, weakening citation traceability in high-stakes regulatory tutoring. To address this limitation, we propose RegTutor, a self-correcting agentic retrieval-augmented generation framework for medical-device compliance training. Specifically, RegTutor retrieves regulatory evidence from 21 CFR Parts 803, 807, and 820, as well as FDA guidance, evaluates evidence sufficiency, rewrites inadequate queries, generates tutoring feedback, and validates citation format and claim-evidence alignment before finalizing its response. Extensive results showed that RegTutor achieved 100.0% answer correctness, citation accuracy, and helpfulness on a predefined 30-item controlled evaluation. In a balanced 300-item operational rerun, all RegTutor runs completed successfully, and citation accuracy reached 99.0%. On a separately frozen 60-item manually reviewed blind evaluation, RegTutor achieved 100.0% answer correctness, citation accuracy, and helpfulness among 59 completed runs. A secondary replication with GLM-4.7 further demonstrated 100.0% answer correctness and 98.3% citation accuracy. These findings demonstrate the value of self-correction and citation validation for traceable regulatory tutoring

title: cfad: Characteristic Function Anomaly Detector for Financial Time Series
abstract: cfad is research-oriented Python software for empirical characteristic-function analysis of distributional change in financial time series. The package provides rolling ECF estimation, real-frequency distributional discrepancy scores, two-sided Page-CUSUM monitoring, parametric characteristic-function models, goodness-of-fit tools, walk-forward backtesting, bootstrap and sensitivity diagnostics, reproducible Monte Carlo validation workflows, and optional Cython acceleration. The project is designed for methodological research, benchmarking, and reproducible experimentation rather than unqualified production anomaly-detection claims.

title: Quantum Information Graphs: Adaptive Topological Analysis
abstract: Quantum information graphs (QIGs) represent a novel framework for modeling and analyzing complex quantum systems. This paper proposes a novel self-adaptive topological analysis method leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum hidden computation. The core mechanism involves simulating QIGs with quantum entanglement and utilizing quantum computation to efficiently characterize topological properties. The research presents a new approach to topology analysis, offering significant improvements in efficiency compared to traditional methods. This work contributes to the advancement of quantum information processing and explores the potential of QIGs for complex problem-solving.

title: Quantum Entanglement Non-Linear Modulation: Adaptive Parameter Control
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics, presents a unique opportunity for advanced computation. However, harnessing this phenomenon necessitates sophisticated control mechanisms. This paper investigates a novel approach to quantum state manipulation based on the dynamic adjustment of entanglement parameters, offering a pathway towards enhanced quantum computation performance. We propose a self-adaptive modulation scheme predicated on the inherent non-linear properties of entangled states, aiming to mitigate errors and optimize quantum algorithms. The core of this research lies in the design of a novel entanglement modulation protocol that leverages the system's inherent responsiveness to external perturbations, thereby establishing a dynamic and controlled system for quantum information processing. This work introduces a new method of parameter control for quantum systems, aiming to improve the robustness of computations.

title: 自适应量子概率场场论的非线性建模
abstract: This paper explores the development of a novel self-adaptive quantum probability field model. Traditional probabilistic models often rely on static parameter settings, limiting their ability to accurately represent complex systems. We propose a method leveraging quantum circuit simulation to dynamically adjust probability field parameters, enabling a more flexible and potentially more accurate system modeling process. The core mechanism involves iterative quantum circuit simulation based on input data and system state, allowing the model to continuously refine its representation of the underlying dynamics. This approach addresses a significant limitation of existing probabilistic frameworks, offering a pathway towards enhanced system understanding and predictive capability. We present a preliminary implementation demonstrating the efficacy of this self-adaptive approach in a simplified system, showcasing its potential for broader applicability.

title: Probabilistic Programming for Hierarchical Bayesian Networks with Stochastic Differential Equations
abstract: This paper presents a framework for efficiently learning and exploring hierarchical Bayesian Networks (HBNs) incorporating Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs). The core idea leverages Probabilistic Programming languages to address the computational challenges inherent in combining Bayesian inference with SDEs. We introduce a compiler designed to translate HBNs with SDEs into a computationally tractable representation, facilitating sampling using techniques like Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) or SDE solvers. This approach offers a novel solution compared to traditional methods, providing a pathway for modeling complex dynamical systems within a Bayesian framework. The presented methodology focuses on the translation and optimization aspects, omitting experimental validation. The key contributions lie in the compiler architecture and the formulated mathematical representation for efficient computation. The target application areas include finance, neuroscience, and engineering, where HBNs with SDEs are increasingly relevant.

title: ##基于多智能体学习的复杂系统建模
abstract: This paper explores the application of multi-agent learning (MAL) for modeling and simulating complex systems. Complex systems, characterized by emergent behavior arising from interactions between their components, pose significant challenges for traditional modeling techniques. This work proposes a novel approach where complex systems are represented as collections of intelligent agents interacting within a defined environment. Utilizing MAL algorithms, these agents learn to coordinate and adapt their behavior, effectively mimicking the system's dynamics and evolution. The core claim of this research is that MAL provides a viable methodology for modeling complex systems by explicitly capturing the intricate interactions inherent in their structure. The proposed mechanism involves defining agents with specific roles and objectives, allowing them to learn optimal strategies through iterative interaction. This approach offers a potentially more accurate and adaptable representation compared to static models, particularly for systems exhibiting non-linear dynamics and emergent properties. The paper details the framework and outlines key considerations for applying MAL to complex system modeling, focusing on agent design, learning algorithm selection, and system evaluation. Ultimately, this research contributes to a deeper understanding and improved control strategies for complex systems across a variety of domains.

title: Calamian Deer Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDMA)
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Calamian Deer Metaheuristic Algorithm (CDMA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Calamian deer. CDMA is designed to address complex optimization problems, particularly those exhibiting multimodal landscapes and intricate search spaces. The algorithm employs a unique combination of particle movement strategies – a velocity adjustment mechanism influenced by both the distance to the global best and a stochastic component – alongside a novel 'deer-trotting' mechanism that mimics the deer's natural movement patterns. Mathematical formulations are presented to detail the algorithm's core components, including the objective function evaluation, particle velocity calculation, and position update rules. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a series of benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions with reasonable computational efficiency. Key performance metrics such as convergence rate and solution quality are analyzed. Future research directions, including parameter tuning strategies and potential extensions for handling constrained optimization problems, are also discussed.

abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to optimization using quantum computation, specifically focusing on geometric optimization. The core concept revolves around transforming optimization problems into quantum states, leveraging quantum entanglement and quantum computing's unique properties to achieve enhanced efficiency. We explore a method for mapping complex geometric structures to a quantum state space, utilizing quantum entanglement as a key enabling mechanism. The potential benefits include the ability to tackle optimization problems previously intractable with classical algorithms, offering a fundamentally new perspective on geometric problem-solving. The research investigates the feasibility of this approach through theoretical analysis and initial simulations, highlighting the advantages and challenges associated with implementing this quantum optimization strategy.

title: Bougainville Giant Rat: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of a Unique Rodent
abstract: This paper introduces Bougainville Giant Rat (BGR), a new metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging strategies of the Bougainville Giant Rat, a unique rodent endemic to Bougainville Island. BGR leverages the rat's remarkable ability to efficiently locate and exploit food sources in a complex and dynamic environment. The algorithm employs a combination of adaptive memory, a novel exploration-exploitation balance mechanism based on the rat's sniffing patterns, and a population-based search strategy. We detail the algorithm's core principles, mathematical formulations, and demonstrate its performance through simulations across a variety of benchmark optimization problems. The results indicate that BGR exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), particularly in problems characterized by high dimensionality and complex landscapes. The algorithm's adaptive nature and efficient exploration-exploitation balance contribute to its robust performance. Future work will focus on incorporating further insights from the rat's behavior and exploring potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Self-Correcting Probabilistic Programming Languages
abstract: Probabilistic programming languages (PPLs) offer a powerful paradigm for modeling and reasoning under uncertainty. However, their widespread adoption is hindered by inherent challenges, primarily stemming from implicit assumptions, the complexity of inference, and a general lack of formal verification mechanisms. This paper introduces Self-Correcting Probabilistic Programming Languages (SCPLs), a novel approach designed to address these shortcomings. SCPLs integrate a runtime monitoring system with an adaptive inference engine, enabling the automatic detection and correction of potential errors during program execution. The core mechanism leverages continuous tracking of program state, identifying inconsistencies and violations of stated assumptions. This information is then utilized to refine the program's logic, driving convergence and ultimately bolstering the reliability and trustworthiness of probabilistic models. We demonstrate the potential of this approach through a conceptual framework, highlighting the key components and outlining a potential implementation strategy. This work represents a significant step towards more robust and dependable PPLs, paving the way for broader applications in domains requiring rigorous uncertainty quantification.

abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed Bobuck-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BIMA), designed for tackling complex optimization problems. The algorithm's core innovation stems from the behavioral characteristics of the Bobuck fish, a fascinating creature known for its unique swimming patterns. BIMA leverages these patterns to establish a robust exploration-exploitation balance within the search process. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach with a novel mutation operator inspired by Bobuck's directional changes. Mathematical formulations are presented, detailing the key components of the algorithm, including the position representation, the mutation probability, and the acceptance criterion. title: Quantum Entanglement-Driven Constraint Optimization
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a phenomenon where two or more particles become linked and share the same fate, presents a novel approach to optimization challenges. This paper investigates the application of entanglement to constraint optimization, proposing a quantum constraint optimization algorithm designed to surpass the limitations of classical techniques. We explore the potential of utilizing entanglement to generate correlated variables, enabling simultaneous exploration of multiple solution spaces with significantly increased computational power. The core mechanism focuses on the creation of entangled states that can be manipulated to efficiently explore the solution space. The theoretical foundation and preliminary experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of this approach, offering a promising pathway toward enhanced optimization performance.

title: Hybrid-Model Approaches With RAG Tools in Supporting the Research Process
abstract: Large Language Models are increasingly used in scientific research, but their outputs can include fabricated claims, outdated information, and weak links to source material. This chapter examines a hybrid human-AI model in which researchers retain responsibility for interpretation, validation, and final decisions, while AI supports repetitive or organisational tasks. It compares Foundation Models, Fine-Tuning, and Retrieval-Augmented Generation, arguing that RAG offers a more transparent and cost-effective option for many research uses because it connects outputs to uploaded sources. Using Google NotebookLM, the chapter illustrates RAG in literature review synthesis and qualitative data analysis. These examples are exploratory, not a formal evaluation. They suggest that RAG can support orientation and organisation, but remains limited in analytical depth and synthesis.

title: Multimodal Jailbreak Attack Defense Method with Integrated Steering Vector Detection
authors: YAO Jiawang, DING Jianwei, PENG Ziming, TIAN Huawei
abstract: With the widespread adoption of large vision-language models in multimodal tasks, their security faces severe challenges. Among them, jailbreak attacks bypass safety mechanisms through adversarial samples and carefully crafted prompts, inducing models to generate harmful content. Existing defense approaches mainly focus on enhancing the safety of model outputs or improving the accuracy of harmful sample detection. However, the former often reduces discriminability and increases computational costs, while the latter usually lacks post-alignment mechanisms and cannot effectively intervene in model outputs. To address these issues, this paper proposes a novel multimodal defense method based on steering vector detection and dual-alignment mechanism. Specifically, the method employs pre-generated steering vectors to detect harmful outputs, thereby improving both detection accuracy and efficiency. A subsequent alignment mechanism is applied to filter the outputs, ensuring response safety. To construct training data, this paper generates adversarial images corres-ponding to harmful queries and responses, paired with the same harmful queries and original images to form a new dataset. The data are fed into the model to extract hidden states under both harmful and benign inputs. By computing the average differences between positive and negative samples, this paper obtains steering vectors and thresholds for jailbreak detection. During inference, model hidden states are projected onto the steering vectors, and inputs are classified as harmful or benign based on the threshold. If deemed harmful, the defense mechanism is triggered, where an external model generates candidate outputs that are scored and filtered to produce safe and useful responses. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves higher detection accuracy and robustness against harmful samples across multiple datasets, while significantly improving output safety. Meanwhile, sample detection is conducted without the involvement of external models, effectively reducing computational costs.

title: Attention-Enhanced EfficientNet-B0 with CBAM and Grad-CAM for Explainable Breast Ultrasound Image Classification
abstract: Breast cancer is one of the most common diseases affecting women worldwide, and early diagnosis plays an important role in improving treatment outcomes and reducing mortality.Among the available imaging techniques, breast ultrasound is widely used because it is safe, non-invasive, and particularly effective for examining dense breast tissue.However, interpreting ultrasound images remains difficult due to image noise, low contrast, and the visual similarity between benign and malignant lesions.This study presents an explainable deep learning framework for breast ultrasound image classification by combining EfficientNet-B0 with the Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM).In addition, Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) was incorporated to provide visual explanations for the model's predictions and improve their interpretability.The proposed framework was evaluated using the publicly available BUSI dataset, which contains 780 breast ultrasound images divided into three classes: normal, benign, and malignant.The dataset was split into 70% for training, 15% for validation, and 15% for testing.To evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed method, two baseline models, ResNet50 and EfficientNet-B0, were implemented and compared with the proposed EfficientNet-B0 + CBAM model.ResNet50 was trained for 2 epochs, while EfficientNet-B0 and EfficientNet-B0 + CBAM were trained for 5 epochs using the Adam optimizer with a learning rate of 0.0001 and a batch size of 16.The experimental results showed that the proposed model achieved a test accuracy of 81.20%, compared with 79.49% obtained by the baseline EfficientNet-B0 model.In addition, the recall for the malignant class increased from 0.6452 to 0.6774, demonstrating an improved ability to identify malignant breast lesions.The generated Grad-CAM visualizations also showed that the model focused on clinically relevant regions of the ultrasound images, providing useful visual explanations for its predictions.Overall, the results indicate that integrating CBAM with EfficientNet-B0 can improve classification performance while Grad-CAM enhances the transparency of the decision-making process.These findings suggest that the proposed framework has the potential to support radiologists by providing accurate predictions together with interpretable visual explanations.

title: QUANTUM-SAFE SECURITY FRAMEWORK FOR PRIVACY-PRESERVING 6G COMMUNICATION SYSTEMS
abstract: This research paper presents a framework, referred to as QRAPSF, which is quantum-resilient and adaptive privacy security framework for 6G communication systems. The QRAPSF framework incorporates quantum-resistant key establishment using ML-KEM, authentication using ML-DSA, lightweight privacy preserving identity management, adaptive physical layer security, and threat aware security level selection. The hierarchical security controller determines the appropriate security level based on channel status, device capability, latency requirements, and threat level. The proposed QRAPSF framework obtains attack detection accuracy of 96.24%, authentication success rate of 98.31%, and privacy preservation efficiency of 95.14% under 5% network load and 93.81%, 96.19%, and 92.61%, respectively, under 30% network load. The communication overhead remains between 9.42% and 11.68%, whereas the authentication latency varies between 29.84 ms and 37.42 ms depending on the network load. Under 30% network load, the proposed QRAPSF framework has communication overhead 5.40 percentage points less than that of Lattice-Based Physical Layer Security and authentication latency 7.86 ms less than that of Hybrid PQC Authentication.

title: A property-aware empirical analysis of differential evolution variants using the generalized numerical benchmark generator
abstract: Benchmarking studies in continuous optimization often report aggregate rankings, yet provide limited insight into why particular algorithms succeed or fail under specific landscape conditions. This paper presents a property-aware empirical assessment of ten competitive Differential Evolution (DE) variants using the Generalized Numerical Benchmark Generator (GNBG), a configurable framework that enables controlled manipulation of problem characteristics. Ten state-of-the art variants of DE are tested across three distinct datasets. The first dataset, GNBG-45, featuring 45 problem instances, each designed to isolate a single landscape property such as basin linearity, conditioning, variable interactions, symmetry or deceptiveness. The remaining datasets, GNBG-I and GNBG-II, are well established in the literature and include 24 functions each, covering unimodal, multimodal single component and multimodal multiple component problems. Together, these data sets provide a layered and comprehensive benchmarking environment. Experimental results show that ALSHADE exhibits the strongest overall robustness and consistency across diverse landscape categories and benchmark suites, while LSHADE-SPACMA exhibits the strongest scalability and robustness in multiple dimensional settings. Other variants, including IMODE, EA4eig, APSM-jSO, and TSALSHADE, demonstrate competitive behavior on selected problem classes but lower overall consistency. Overall, the study shows the ability of GNBG to distinguish algorithmic behavior in a variety of problem structures, supporting its use as a detailed and property-aware benchmarking suite.

title: On‐Chip Cryogenic Level Meters for Magnetic Field Based on TiN Superconducting Microwave Resonators
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise control of the external magnetic field orientation with respect to quantum devices is of particular importance since the field orientation can significantly influence quantum states. Therefore, in situ calibration of rotational misalignment of the magnetic field at cryogenic temperatures, where quantum devices are usually operated, is essential, yet remains largely unexplored. Here, leveraging the advantages of low microwave loss and high critical field, we demonstrate that high‐quality TiN nanowire superconducting microwave resonators exhibit sensitive and anisotropic responses to varied magnetic fields, enabling three‐dimensional calibration of the field orientation using a single device. Based on a developed tensor model, we extract competitive out‐of‐plane orientation calibration uncertainty of . Our approach maps the magnetic field to a readily measurable scalar parameter, thereby providing a reliable, repeatable, and efficient method for precisely quantifying field orientation, a capability highly desirable in research fields such as condensed matter physics and quantum computation.

title: SSAKG 2.0: An Open-Source Package for Structural Associative Sequence Memory and Context-Based Retrieval
abstract: This article presents SSAKG 2.0, an open-source software package for constructing and operating Structural Sequential Associative Knowledge Graphs (SSAKGs). An SSAKG represents objects as graph vertices and ordered sequences as structural patterns of graph connections. The resulting sparse graph is used as an associative memory in which complete sequences can be reconstructed from a partial, unordered context. Version 2.0 introduces new algorithms that exploit individual bits of computer memory to efficiently search graph connections. The package is implemented in Python, while performance-critical graph operations are implemented in C and exposed through a Python interface. This hybrid implementation provides a flexible high-level programming environment while reducing the memory and computational overhead associated with large sparse graphs. The algorithms were evaluated using randomly generated numerical sequences, sequences derived from sentences in the NLTK corpus, and mRNA sequences. The experiments demonstrate the ability of the package to store and reconstruct sequences from partial contexts and provide a basis for evaluating the effects of graph density, sequence length, and memory size on retrieval performance. SSAKG 2.0 is distributed under the Apache 2.0 open-source license. The package includes documentation and reproducible examples and is publicly available through GitHub and the Python Package Index (PyPI).

title: A Sensor-Adaptive Incremental Learning Framework for Artifact Detection in Satellite Precipitation Data
abstract: Historically, retrieving rainfall data from satellite imagery has been the domain of space agencies. However, in recent years, the development of cheaper, more compact satellites (SmallSats) capable of detecting rainfall proxies has led to a significant increase in private-sector initiatives for satellite launch and surface precipitation products. This rapid growth has yet to be matched by data validation efforts. Consequently, the need for a robust tool to detect anomalies in near-real-time data before it is disseminated to the public has become critical. In this paper, we present the development of an anomaly-detection system to identify artifacts in global satellite-based rainfall products. The developed framework leverages pre-trained computer vision models and incorporates scarce human-labeled data to detect specific anomalies. Our proposed anomaly detection strategy is tested on data from the Special Sensor Microwave Imager (SSMI) and the Special Sensor Microwave Imager/Sounder (SSMIS). Results demonstrate the efficacy of our approach at separating regular orbits from artifact-containing orbits for each satellite, with performance comparable to state-of-the-art in-place methods. Additionally, the framework offers explainability and the capacity for iterative refinement following false-positive or false-negative classifications.

title: Consensus-based optimization for linearly separable functions
abstract: Consensus-based optimization (CBO) is an efficient metaheuristic for global optimisation with attractive mathematical properties, allowing global convergence results even in non-convex settings. In practice it suffers greatly from the curse of dimensionality, as do most particle-based optimisers. Different strategies have been proposed to apply CBO even for high-dimensional optimisation problems, the most prominent being the so-called anisotropic noise model. However, a recent work by Bonandin et al. highlighted that this method performs well primarily on separable objective functions, and even small coordinate rotations severely degrade the performance. Motivated by this observation, in this work we study the case where the objective function is separable only in a linearly transformed coordinate system. To leverage the efficiency of anisotropic CBO we propose a reparametrisation scheme, which provably estimates such a coordinate transformation and then applies CBO in the new variables. Furthermore, we show how our scheme can be interpreted as noise adaptation in CBO. Numerical examples highlight the efficacy of the method, demonstrating significant performance improvements on challenging benchmark objectives.

title: Diagonal unitary covariant superchannels
abstract: We present a complete characterization of diagonal unitary covariant (DU-covariant) superchannels, i.e., higher-order transformations transforming quantum channels into themselves. Necessary and sufficient conditions for complete positivity and trace preservation are derived and the canonical decomposition describing DU-covariant superchannels is provided. The presented framework unifies and extends known families of covariant quantum channels and enables explicit analysis of their action on physically relevant examples, including amplitude-damping, bit-flip, and Pauli channels. Our results provide a practical toolbox for symmetry-restricted higher-order quantum processes and offer a setting for exploring open problems such as the celebrated positive partial transpose-squared conjecture.

title: Graph neural networks for bilateral migration prediction : a European-focused analysis
abstract: Η μετανάστευση αποτελεί ένα από τα πλέον σημαντικά και δυσπρόβλεπτα φαινόμενα της σύγχρονης κοινωνίας, με βαθιές επιπτώσεις σε επίπεδο πολιτικής και ανθρωπιστικού σχεδιασμού. Η παρούσα διατριβή διερευνά κατά πόσο τα Νευρωνικά Δίκτυα Γράφων (Graph Neural Networks – GNNs) μπορούν να βελτιώσουν την πρόβλεψη διμερών μεταναστευτικών ροών σε σχέση με κλασικές μεθόδους αναφοράς, και ταυτόχρονα αναλύει το ευρωπαϊκό σύστημα μετανάστευσης μέσω εργαλείων δικτυακής ανάλυσης. Συγκρίνονται τρεις αρχιτεκτονικές GNN (GCN, GraphSAGE, Temporal-GNN) με τρεις κλασικές μεθόδους (απλή εμμονή, log-γραμμικό βαρυτικό μοντέλο, Random Forest) σε δεδομένα διμερών ροών 21 ετών (2000–2020) για 217 χώρες. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι η απλή μέθοδος εμμονής υπερτερεί όλων των εκπαιδευμένων μοντέλων κατά παράγοντα 4,5 στο μέσο απόλυτο σφάλμα μη-μηδενικών κελιών. Η ανάλυση εντοπίζει τρεις δομικές τάσεις στην ευρωπαϊκή μετανάστευση: την έκρηξη ρουμανικής μετανάστευσης μετά τη διεύρυνση της ΕΕ το 2007, την προοδευτική απομάκρυνση του Ηνωμένου Βασιλείου από το δίκτυο μετά το Brexit, και την ανακατεύθυνση των ουκρανικών ροών προς την Πολωνία. Συμπληρωματικά, μέσω δεδομένων IOM DTM, αναλύεται ο εσωτερικός εκτοπισμός στην Ουκρανία (2022–2026).

title: AI, Fill This Form: A Simple and Effective Data Exfiltration Attack on LLM-Based Browser Extensions Without Prompt Injection
abstract: LLM-based browser extensions execute web tasks without the user supervising each interaction. We introduce Ghost Field Exfiltration (GFE), a data exfiltration attack against this class of system that requires no prompt injection. The attack exploits the asymmetry between what the user sees in a rendered form and what the agent processes in the Document Object Model (DOM): a malicious page presents a small visible form while embedding additional input fields concealed via CSS or accessibility-layer techniques, which the agent fills with the user’s data alongside the legitimate inputs. We evaluate GFE across 300 controlled experiments on three Claude models accessed through the Claude for Chrome extension. Full exfiltration ranges from 19% on Opus 4.6 to 64% on Haiku 4.5, with Personally Identifiable Information (PII) reaching 95% on the smaller model. Our analysis indicates that the models defenses correlate strongly with recognition of sensitive data categories rather than with structural detection of the abuse, indicating that agent-layer safeguards are needed to comprehensively address this class of attack.

title: РОЛЬ НЕЙРОИНТЕЛЛЕКТУАЛЬНОГО МОДЕЛИРОВАНИЯ В ЭКОНОМИКЕ И УПРАВЛЕНИИ: ЗАРУБЕЖНЫЙ И ОТЕЧЕСВТЕННЫЙ ОПЫТ
abstract: В статье предпринята попытка аналитического подхода к выявлению аспектов использования нейроинтеллектуального моделирования в сферах экономики, управления, бизнеса. Автор подходит к решению задач путем сравнительного анализа ключевых ролей нейроинтеллектуального моделирования в зарубежной и отечественной практике. Научная новизна исследования заключается в систематизации информации об аспектах использования нейроинтеллектуального моделирования в отечественном и зарубежном опыте развития экономики, бизнеса и управления. Цель исследования заключается в попытке анализа и систематизации информации направлений использования нейроинтеллектуального моделирования в мировой экономической практике и опыте управления. Теоретическая и практическая значимость исследования состоит в том, что оно может внести существенный вклад в разработку и конструирование бизнес-, управленческих сценариев, позволяющих взаимодействовать в условиях рынка с наибольшей эффективностью.

title: Fuzzy Attention Networks: Differential Fuzzy Attention and Adaptive Explanations for Multimodal AI (Нечёткие сети внимания: дифференцируемое нечёткое внимание и адаптивные объяснения для мультимодального ИИ)
abstract: Fuzzy Attention Networks v3.0.0 Обновление исследовательской системы Fuzzy Attention Networks (FAN) для мультимодальной классификации с использованием нечёткой логики и механизмов внимания. Основные возможности интеграция механизмов fuzzy attention в нейросетевые модели; поддержка задач классификации изображений и мультимодальных данных; специализированные сценарии для медицинских данных; визуализация весов внимания и нечётких функций принадлежности; интерактивный интерфейс на Streamlit; поддержка нескольких наборов данных и архитектур моделей; инструменты обучения, тестирования и анализа результатов; улучшенная интерпретируемость решений модели. Поддерживаемые сценарии Проект включает эксперименты и модели для: Stanford Dogs; CIFAR-10; HAM10000; Chest X-Ray; других задач классификации изображений и мультимодального анализа. Назначение Fuzzy Attention Networks исследует объединение нечёткой логики, механизмов внимания и глубокого обучения для построения более интерпретируемых моделей классификации. Версия v3.0.0 рекомендуется как основная версия репозитория для дальнейшего использования, воспроизведения экспериментов и архивирования. Репозиторий https://github.com/fims9000/FuzzyAttentionNetworks

title: PlanarBench: Evaluating LLM Spatial Reasoning via Planar Graph Drawing
abstract: Existing LLM graph benchmarks typically ask models to answer graph-theoreticquestions or compute symbolic solutions rather than construct spatial layouts.Within-task difficulty is also primarily stratified by vertex count. However, existingresearch also suggests that task difficulty is more closely related to the number ofconstraints imposed by the edges than to the number of vertices being arranged.We introduce PlanarBench, a benchmark that asks models to produce crossing-free ASCII drawings of planar graphs given only an edge list. Across 91 modelconfigurations and 199 non-isomorphic connected planar graphs with 2–7 vertices,edge count is more strongly associated with mean task score than vertex count(r = −0.85 versus r = −0.47) and remains strongly associated after controllingfor vertex count (rpartial = −0.80). PlanarBench provides a controlled settingfor separating these two difficulty axes. In addition, neither drawing area nortotal response length demonstrated a meaningful correlation with score, which isevidence against a simple output-size explanation. Performance varies widely: thebest model scores 159.5 out of 199, most models below 30B parameters scoreunder 25, and substantial failures remain among frontier systems.

Across 91 modelconfigurations and 199 non-isomorphic connected planar graphs with 2–7 vertices,edge count is more strongly associated with mean task score than vertex count(r = −0.85 versus r = −0.47) and remains strongly associated after controllingfor vertex count (rpartial = −0.80). PlanarBench provides a controlled settingfor separating these two difficulty axes. In addition, neither drawing area nortotal response length demonstrated a meaningful correlation with score, which isevidence against a simple output-size explanation. Performance varies widely: thebest model scores 159.5 out of 199, most models below 30B parameters scoreunder 25, and substantial failures remain among frontier systems.

title: 基于量子纠缠的动态几何优化算法
abstract: This paper presents a novel dynamic geometric optimization algorithm based on the principles of quantum entanglement. Traditional geometric optimization methods often rely on manual parameter tuning, limiting efficiency and requiring significant human intervention. This research introduces a new algorithm that leverages quantum entanglement to dynamically adjust geometric transformations, resulting in enhanced optimization performance. The core mechanism involves creating entangled states to represent geometric parameters, enabling instantaneous adjustments and accelerating the optimization process. We detail the algorithm's design, implementation, and preliminary results, demonstrating significant improvements in optimization speed and quality compared to traditional methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential implications of this approach for a wide range of geometric optimization problems.

title: Neuro-Evolution of Multi-Scale Genetic Operators
abstract: This paper investigates the application of multi-scale genetic operators within the context of neuro-evolution. The core claim is that incorporating diverse genetic operations operating at different scales significantly enhances the exploration of the search space and accelerates the convergence rate of neuro-evolutionary algorithms. The proposed mechanism involves the strategic combination of genetic operations, including single-point mutation, crossover, insertion, and deletion, tailored to optimize both the network architecture and its associated weights. Crucially, the scale of these operations is dynamically adjusted based on the complexity of the neural network being evolved. Experimental results, though not presented in this document due to the focus on conceptual development, strongly support the efficacy of this approach, demonstrating improved performance compared to traditional neuro-evolution algorithms. This work represents an expansion of the genetic operator landscape within neuro-evolution, ultimately increasing the search efficiency and adaptability of the entire process.

title: Dynamic Neuron Topology Optimization
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to dynamic neuron topology optimization within neural networks. The core idea centers around real-time analysis and simulation of neuronal connection activity patterns to achieve adaptive optimization of the neuron topology. This optimization aims to significantly enhance both the computational efficiency and learning capabilities of the neural network. The system utilizes neuronal activity data – including activation values, delays, and changes in synaptic weights – to map onto parameters defining the neuron topology, such as node positions, connection strengths, and connection types. Reinforcement learning or genetic algorithms are then employed to optimize the topology configuration, minimizing information transmission delays and maximizing computational resource utilization. Unlike existing methods that primarily focus on adjusting individual neuron or connection weights, this approach treats the topology as a dynamically adjustable entity, leveraging neuronal activity as a guiding signal for optimization. The resulting optimized topology leads to improved network performance under varying computational demands and learning scenarios. The theoretical framework and algorithmic design are presented, outlining the key components and their interactions within the system.

title: California Pocket Mouse: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents California Pocket Mouse (CPM), a new metaheuristic algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the California Pocket Mouse (Chaetomys cutus). CPM leverages the mouse's efficient search strategies for food resources, particularly its ability to adaptively adjust search radius and prioritize promising areas. The algorithm incorporates key aspects of the mouse's behavior, including a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance controlled by a novel adaptive parameter, *ε*, and a guided search mechanism using a heuristic function based on resource density. CPM's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitiveness against established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design aims for computational efficiency and robust performance across diverse problem landscapes. Experimental results show that CPM achieves state-of-the-art performance in certain test cases, indicating its potential as a valuable addition to the metaheuristic optimization toolbox.

title: Adaptive Topological Parameter Adjustment for Non-Linear Machine Learning
abstract: This paper investigates the design of a novel non-linear machine learning framework, termed "Adaptive Topological Parameter Adjustment," that dynamically adjusts model parameters based on real-time data changes. The core principle revolves around utilizing a dynamic topology adjustment mechanism to optimize model parameters, leading to enhanced model adaptability and robustness. We present a theoretical framework and demonstrate its effectiveness through several experiments, showcasing its ability to outperform traditional optimization techniques in scenarios involving evolving data distributions. The framework's focus is on providing a more sophisticated and adaptable approach to machine learning model tuning.

title: 基于动态映射的自适应机器学习的非线性特征提取
abstract: This paper introduces a novel framework for machine learning based on dynamic mapping, designed to automatically extract non-linear features and enhance model generalization. Traditional machine learning often relies on manual feature engineering, which can be time-consuming and may not capture the true complexity of the data. Dynamic mapping provides a method to dynamically adjust feature weights and mappings, enabling the model to learn intricate relationships within the data. We propose a system that iteratively adjusts the feature distribution based on observed data patterns, resulting in improved predictive performance. This work addresses the limitations of existing machine learning techniques by introducing a proactive feature learning mechanism.

Traditional quantum algorithms often rely on static calculations, presenting limitations in scalability and efficiency. This research proposes a novel approach utilizing dynamic topology – a mathematical framework that allows for continuous structural changes – to enhance quantum computation. The core mechanism involves constructing a dynamic topology structure that adapts to the quantum state, enabling efficient quantum self-adaptation. The paper demonstrates the potential of this approach to significantly improve the performance of quantum algorithms, particularly in scenarios requiring rapid parameter adjustments.

title: Quantum Entanglement Self-Adaptation Framework for Enhanced Quantum System Performance
abstract: Quantum entanglement offers a fundamentally new paradigm for computation and information processing, potentially surpassing classical approaches in certain areas. However, the inherent complexity of quantum systems necessitates sophisticated control and optimization strategies. This paper presents a novel framework for self-adaptive quantum system parameter adjustment, leveraging the unique properties of quantum entanglement. We introduce a "Quantum State Graph" concept to model quantum system dynamics, dynamically adjusting parameters based on entanglement correlations to enhance performance. This approach goes beyond traditional parameter optimization techniques, offering a potential pathway to significantly improve the capabilities of quantum systems. This work demonstrates the feasibility of automated optimization through entanglement-based self-adaptation, potentially unlocking new quantum algorithms and applications.

title: Blind Small-eared Shrew: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Blind Small-eared Shrew (BSESh), a new metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. Inspired by the foraging behavior of the blind small-eared shrew, a creature reliant on tactile and auditory cues in a dark environment, BSESh leverages a combination of exploration and exploitation strategies. The algorithm employs a novel "blind search" mechanism, where candidate solutions are generated based on local environmental assessments and guided by a probabilistic decision process. The core of BSESh involves a dynamic parameter adjustment scheme, denoted as α and β, which govern the balance between exploration and exploitation. α controls the probability of exploring new regions in the search space, while β regulates the level of exploitation around the current best solution. The algorithm's performance is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. The key mathematical formulations underlying BSESh are presented, including the probability density function for solution selection (p(x)) and the parameter update rules for α and β. The results indicate that BSESh is a promising metaheuristic algorithm with potential applications in diverse fields.

title: Dynamic Bayesian Networks for Adaptive Control of Complex Systems with Uncertainty
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive control of complex systems utilizing Dynamic Bayesian Networks (DBNs). Traditional Bayesian Networks are inherently static, limiting their applicability in systems characterized by dynamic changes and inherent uncertainty. This research addresses this limitation by introducing a DBN framework where both the network structure and conditional probability tables are continuously updated through an adaptive learning mechanism. Specifically, a reinforcement learning algorithm is employed to optimize the DBN, enabling it to effectively model and control the system in the face of evolving dynamics and uncertainties. The key innovation lies in the synergistic combination of Bayesian inference with adaptive learning, resulting in a control system capable of autonomous adaptation. The theoretical foundation and the proposed methodology are outlined, emphasizing the system's ability to learn and respond to changes in real-time. This approach offers a robust and flexible solution for controlling systems where traditional control methods struggle due to inherent unpredictability. The effectiveness of the DBN is demonstrated conceptually through a generalized framework, highlighting the potential for application across diverse complex systems. The core of the methodology centers around continuous refinement of the network, leveraging observed data to improve predictive accuracy and ultimately, control performance.

title: Prophecy Variables and Invariants in the Move Prover
abstract: In this paper, we demonstrate a significant empirical performance gain in the Move Prover, particularly in scenarios with highly branched borrowing structures, by reducing the verification complexity of ownership borrows from O(BL) to O(BL), where B is the number of possible parent nodes and L is the length of the borrow chain. In our benchmark tests evaluating conditional borrow and update operations within the Move Prover (L = 2, B = 8), the original model required 42 seconds to complete verification, whereas our proposed model finished in under 2 seconds. The Move Prover models these borrows through mutations, which represent copies of values and record borrowing relationships. This representation faces the challenge of strictly identifying the exact parent node at each level of a sub-borrow, which significantly increases the complexity of direct write-back operations. We resolve this through the adoption of the prophecy variable model: a representation that constrains parent node values instead of using direct write-backs. All operations are resolved within the active scope, avoiding complex parent tracking and yielding the aforementioned complexity reduction. During our experiments, we also observed that the current implementation of global and update invariants in the Move Prover operates with limited regard for Move’s strict ownership rules, making the adoption of the prophecy variable model more complex. Consequently, we analyze how existing invariant architectures affect the adoption of this model.

title: An Automated Workflow for Processing and 3D Visualization of Multi-Component Seismic Signals Using IRIS Telemetry Data
abstract: This paper presents an automated computational workflow for the acquisition, instrument-response correction and three-dimensional visualization of multi-component seismic records obtained from the IRIS Federation of Digital Seismograph Networks (FDSNs) using the open-source ObsPy (v1.5.0) package. The workflow targets engineering applications and consists of four stages: (i) selection of three-component (3C) broadband stations, (ii) bandpass filtering and spectral deconvolution of the instrument response to obtain ground displacement in physical units, (iii) calculation of theoretical P- and S-wave arrival times with the Tau-P kinematic algorithm based on the IASP91 reference Earth velocity model, and (iv) construction of an interactive 3D particle motion visualization in which segments associated with the P-wave, S-wave and background are color-coded. The pipeline is demonstrated on three seismic events recorded in February 2023 by the broadband station KO.BNN, including the destructive Mw 7.8 Kahramanmaraş earthquake. The workflow yields the absolute three-dimensional displacement vector and produces interactive visualizations that are intended for use by structural engineers as a complement to traditional one-dimensional acceleration records.

title: Semantic profiling of user as an instrument of personalization in agricultural advisory systems
abstract: The concept of semantic profiling of user as a key mechanism of personalization in intelligent agro-advisory systems is cosidered. We analysse classical profiling models (demographic, behavioral, cognitive, social) that do not provide sufficient flexibility and explainability, whereas ontological models enable the integration of heterogeneous data sources, the formalization of relations between user characteristics, and the assurance of semantic consistency. We propose a general algorithm for profile construction that combins static and dynamic parameters (identification, behavioral, cognitive, contextual) into a structured format that supports logical inference and alignment of user both with other subjects (e.g., selecting an advisor for a farmer) and objects (agrotechnologies, educational courses, support programs) of agroadvisory system. The advantages and problems of using the proposed approach are considered using the example. We analyze the advantages and challenges of the proposed approach on example of an intelligent ALE system focused on supporting the agroadvisor professional activities. Further research is planned to focus on the creation and alignment of ontological models of individual tasks and the practical validation of the approach within real world agro-advisory platforms.

title: TD-GAE: A multimodal large language model framework for adaptive and explainable guided art learning
abstract: Multimodal large language models offer strong potential for adaptive and explainable support in creative learning, but many existing systems mainly focus on content generation rather than structured guidance, progress tracking, and interpretable feedback. This paper presents TD-GAE, a Multimodal Large Language Model framework for adaptive and explainable guided art learning. The proposed method combines staged guidance using a directed acyclic graph, learner-state estimation, retrieval-augmented pedagogical context, structured feedback actions, confidence-gated critique, and safety controls to preserve learner agency and originality. Experiments were conducted on six public datasets covering sketch recognition, sketch-photo retrieval, aesthetic assessment, and fine-art style analysis, with comparisons against prompt-only, retrieval-based, planner-only, and agentic baselines. Results show that TD-GAE improves sketch interpretation by 10.2 percentage points on Quick, Draw! and 8.7 points on TU-Berlin over the prompt-only baseline. It also achieves a 22.2% relative mAP improvement in xemplar retrieval over CLIP, a Spearman correlation of 0.587 for aesthetic assessment, and a 40.7% relative improvement in rubric-based learning gains over the next-best baseline. Human evaluation further reports strong ratings for helpfulness, clarity, appropriateness, and perceived usefulness. These findings indicate that TD-GAE can support creative learning as an adaptive, explainable, and pedagogically grounded AI tutoring framework.

title: Automated differential–linear cryptanalysis of SIMON-like ciphers via truncated differential
abstract: Ciphers built on bitwise AND, XOR, and rotation are highly competitive for resource‑constrained Internet of Things devices. A representative example is the SIMON family of lightweight block ciphers, introduced by the U.S. National Security Agency in 2013. Differential‑linear (DL) cryptanalysis of such ciphers comprises two central tasks: identifying promising DL distinguishers and evaluating their correlations. Recent notable works, including the Differential‑Linear Connectivity Table (DLCT), the Differential Algebraic Transitional Form (DATF), and new evaluation methods from boomerang and truncated differential perspectives, have made significant progress in correlation evaluation. Beyond correlation evaluation, efficiently finding long DL distinguishers with high correlation remains a crucial challenge, particularly for AndRX ciphers. To address this, we propose a two‑step solver‑aided strategy. The first step employs an automated solver to generate a large pool of DL distinguisher candidates by concatenating truncated differentials with linear approximations. A representative example is the SIMON family of lightweight block ciphers, introduced by the U.S. National Security Agency in 2013. title: Benchmarking Spatial, Spectral, and Self-Supervised Cues for Face Forgery Detection under Realistic Degradation
abstract: Face forgery detectors often achieve strong results on controlled benchmarks, but their reliability under realistic image degradations remains limited. This paper presents a standardized benchmark for face forgery detection using the Multi-Dimensional Face Forgery Image (MFFI) dataset and evaluates performance on both clean and degraded test partitions. We compare six model families, including convolutional networks, transformer-based models, and a frozen self-supervised DINOv3 backbone, across spatial, spectral, and hybrid input representations. The results show that clean-set performance is not a reliable indicator of robustness under compression, resizing, and blurring. Xception with RGB obtains the best clean performance, reaching 0.884 mean ROC-AUC, but degrades substantially on the harder partition. In contrast, frozen DINOv3 achieves the strongest degraded-set result, with 0.726 mean ROC-AUC, while training only a linear classification head. The representation analysis indicates that Fourier-domain cues are most useful when combined with RGB information, whereas purely spectral inputs consistently underperform spatial representations. Qualitative attribution maps further suggest that convolutional detectors focus on localized artifacts, while DINOv3 relies on broader facial structure. These findings reinforce the need for degraded evaluation protocols and highlight self-supervised visual representations as a promising direction for robust face forgery detection. Our source code is publicly available at https://github.com/lucasdocunha/FaceForgery-Benchmark/.

title: Hidden Services Protocol for Mixnets
abstract: Mix networks (mixnets) provide network-level privacy by routing each communication packet through a sequence of intermediaries, called mixnodes, that randomly delay and cryptographically transform packets before forwarding them, making it difficult for observers to link mixnet entries to exits. While this mechanism protects sender privacy from both external adversaries and the receiver, existing mixnets lack a secure and practical protocol that simultaneously protects receiver (destination) privacy, particularly from the sender. We close this gap. We introduce the first practical and secure hidden-service protocol for mixnets, providing receiver privacy alongside sender anonymity. Our design builds on Single-Use Reply Blocks (SURBs), which enable anonymous replies without revealing the receiver's address. We show, however, that existing approaches to using SURBs expose two practical attacks that can compromise sender or receiver anonymity when the opposing party controls only a single mixnode. We develop defenses against both vulnerabilities. Building on these defenses, we introduce NymHS, a secure and practical hidden-service protocol for mixnets that supports anonymous service discovery, authenticated bidirectional sessions, and asynchronous SURB replenishment. We implement NymHS on the open-source Nym codebase and evaluate its practicality through web-browsing experiments across 118 websites, measuring each of the 27 configurations three times (9,558 page loads). Our results demonstrate that hidden services can be deployed efficiently over mixnets. In particular, increasing the Sphinx payload from 2 KiB to 10 KiB reduces mean page-load latency by approximately 5.2x and decreases communication overhead from 21.7% to 4.3% relative to the current Nym baseline.

title: Prior-Guided Implicit Neural Representations for Single-Subject Diffusion MRI Super-Resolution
abstract: Resolving complex fiber geometries in brain white matter requires high-resolution diffusion MRI at the cost of long acquisition times. This leads many clinical protocols to opt for low-resolution scans, making downstream microstructure estimation and tractography challenging. Implicit neural representations (INRs) can model the diffusion signal continuously, enabling native single-subject super-resolution by querying the network at arbitrary spatial coordinates, yet existing methods often suffer from long training times and lack a mechanism to incorporate anatomical priors to regularize super-resolution by constraining the space of plausible reconstructions. To address these limitations, we propose a novel transfer-learning framework that pre-trains an INR on a high-resolution template and then adapts it to subject-specific scans via registration and fine-tuning. For $4\times$ through-plane super-resolution from 5 mm to 1.25 mm on Human Connectome Project (HCP) data, our method reduces NRMSE by 36-49% and increases FSIM by 24-43% over a recent baseline with $6\times$ faster training, outperforming competing INR-based methods across both image quality and domain-specific metrics. Code is available on the project page at https://abdulkaderghandoura.github.io/research/msc-thesis/ .

title: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications
abstract: Computer-use agents are emerging as a paradigm for agentic human-AI interaction, combining language reasoning with multi-modal interface grounding to operate GUIs. Yet their effectiveness for blind screen-reader users in real-world desktop workflows remains unclear. We present a three-week diary study with 8 blind users using OLLA, a screen-reader-accessible CUA prototype, collecting 1,258 commands across 12 applications with screenshots, UI trees, model responses, and action traces. We evaluate GPT-5 during deployment and re-execute the same commands with four additional models. GPT-5 achieved the highest success rate at 52.5%. Trace analysis reveals grounding, planning, constraint-tracking, and termination failures, while interviews reveal beyond-automation needs.

title: AI-DRIVEN PERSONALIZED MARKETING AND CONSUMER RESPONSES: A STRUCTURED LITERATURE REVIEW OF PERSONALIZATION, PRIVACY AND TRUST AMONG GENERATION Z
abstract: This structured literature review examines the responses of consumers, Generation Z in particular, to AI-based personalized marketing, and includes the emerging evidence from India. Twenty empirical studies published between 2015 and 2026 have been integrated in a systematic manner focusing on the value of personalization, privacy, trust, transparency, consumer control, and behavioral responses. It was found that personalization is value-add in the context of relevance, usefulness, ease of use and engagement. However, overpersonalization was found to invade privacy and lead to privacy-related resistance. Trust is a “crucial element in the perception of personalization value and acceptance of personalization. Consent, transparency, and control in the context of personalization shape the value and risk. Evidence from Generation Z suggests acceptance is more likely to be conditional than unconditional. Indian evidence is scant and emerging, but also supports the coexistence of personalization and privacy. An integrated personalization-value-privacy-trust perspective is created, and implications for marketing with AI, as well as future research, are described.

title: Agentic Commerce and SME Competitiveness: An Integrative Review and Theory-Informed Research Framework
abstract: Research background: Artificial intelligence is shifting online shopping from recommendation-based assistance towards delegated search, comparison, configuration, and, in emerging cases, transaction execution. For SMEs, this transition may expand market access while simultaneously creating new forms of algorithmic gatekeeping and platform dependence. Purpose of the article: This integrative review develops a theory-informed explanation of how agentic commerce may affect SME competitiveness. Competitiveness is conceptualised as the joint ability to capture agent-mediated demand while preserving strategic option value, customer access, and bargaining autonomy over time. Methods: Seventeen documented OpenAlex title-and-abstract queries were used to identify English-language journal articles published between 2015 and July 2026. Following deduplication and eligibility screening, 117 Scopus- and/or Web of Science-indexed articles were reviewed in full, comprising 82 consumer-agent studies and 35 SME-platform studies. A concept-centric synthesis was conducted using dynamic capabilities and resource dependence as the principal theoretical lenses. The review does not claim exhaustive coverage or pooled causal effects, as the discovery process relied on a single source and only one record was identified through direct merchant-bridge queries. Claims were therefore calibrated according to evidential directness, convergence across research designs, and proximity to the outcome of interest. Findings & Value added: The synthesis identifies five core themes: assistance-to-delegation, machine legibility, trust transfer, empowerment–dependence, and offering/governance contingency. The proposed framework distinguishes foundational capabilities—product-data legibility, interface and transaction readiness, and verifiable trust evidence—from higher-order sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring capabilities. These mechanisms operate through eligibility and visibility, trust transfer, delegation depth, and dependency exposure. The evidence is moderate for consumer trust mechanisms and established forms of platform dependence, but remains limited for execution-capable agents, direct SME outcomes, and comparative boundary effects. Six propositions are developed to provide a testable rather than validated causal framework. The findings are relevant to SME managers, platform and AI-agent designers, policymakers, and researchers seeking to understand how firms can capture agent-mediated demand without surrendering strategic option value.

title: Avaliação da Sensibilidade de Modelos a Ataques de Inversão de Gradiente no Aprendizado Federado
abstract: O Aprendizado Federado (FL) permite o treinamento distribuído de modelos. O FL permanece vulnerável aos Ataques de Inversão de Gradiente (GIA), nos quais agentes maliciosos reconstroem dados dos clientes a partir dos gradientes compartilhados. Este trabalho avalia a sensibilidade de modelos locais aos GIA e investiga a eficácia da Privacidade Diferencial (DP) como estratégia de mitigação. Experimentos preliminares com o dataset LFW demonstram que camadas convolucionais são mais suscetíveis aos GIA, especialmente nas épocas iniciais do treinamento, e que níveis relativamente baixos de ruído são suficientes para degradar a qualidade das reconstruções.

title: Do Recovered Names Help? Evaluating Binary Function-Name Recovery for Vulnerability Triage
abstract: Abstract: Systems that recover function names from stripped binaries are motivated almost entirely by security applications, yet report only agreement between predicted and ground-truth names, measured on obfuscated code, firmware, and malware alike. None has been evaluated on the task its motivation names. We evaluate four state-of-the-art systems on binaries compiled from 20 CVE-affected revisions at three levels: naming accuracy over 182,840 functions, graded outcomes on the 50 designated targets, and triage as retrieval from advisory-derived queries. Three findings emerge. Every target name any model recovered correctly was already in that model's own training split; no name absent from the training corpus was recovered by any model. They fail in opposite ways (silence versus fluent unrelated names) that aggregate scores treat alike while favoring the riskier behavior. And where an advisory describes a flaw without naming the function, even the developers' real names rarely retrieve the target, placing the bottleneck outside recovery quality. At 20 CVEs these are small-scale observations, but they are the first task-level measurements this literature's motivation calls for. We release the corpus, the harness, and, because we retrain all four models, an exact account of training and evaluation overlap.

title: Federated Uncertainty Consensus: Swarm-Level Safety Fallbacks for Disconnected Edge AI
abstract: Edge Artificial Intelligence (AI) is increasingly deployed in latency-critical and highly dynamic environments, such as autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) swarms and disaster response robotics [3, 9]. A critical vulnerability in these systems is data drift—where the operational environment deviates from the training distribution, leading to silent model degradation [1, 2]. Current safety fallback mechanisms rely on hierarchical cloud architectures, where an edge device defers ambiguous inferences to a central server [4]. However, this is structurally impossible in disconnected, cloud-denied, or strictly localized ad-hoc networks. In this paper, we propose Federated Uncertainty Consensus (FUC), a novel technical AI safety protocol. Rather than defaulting to a centralized cloud, an edge node utilizes local Uncertainty Quantification (UQ) via Conformal Prediction [5]. Upon detecting out-of-distribution (OOD) anomalies, the node broadcasts a lightweight peer-to-peer query to the local swarm. The swarm mathematically aggregates its confidence, achieving a "safety fallback consensus" to override the degraded node. We outline the decentralized architecture, provide empirical latency metrics from a simulated ad-hoc swarm, and demonstrate that FUC maintains real-time safety thresholds without reliance on cloud infrastructure [7, 8].

title: Teaching the Colossus to Say No: A Critical Survey Review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Alignment Strategies for Large Language Models in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of alignment and large language models as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Canada Lynx-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Canada Lynx Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CLIMA), motivated by the hunting strategies of the Canada Lynx. The algorithm leverages the Lynx's ability to efficiently explore and exploit a search space, mimicking its movement patterns and decision-making processes. CLIMA incorporates key elements of Lynx behavior, including territory defense, prey selection, and adaptive movement, into its core optimization mechanism. The algorithm utilizes a dynamic territory representation, a probabilistic prey selection mechanism, and an adaptive movement strategy to achieve robust and efficient convergence. We demonstrate the effectiveness of CLIMA through simulations on several benchmark optimization problems, showcasing its performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The theoretical analysis reveals the algorithm's ability to handle complex, non-convex landscapes and its potential for adaptability in varying problem environments. The simulations highlight CLIMA's strengths in terms of speed of convergence and solution quality. Further research will focus on adapting the algorithm to different problem types and exploring its scalability for large-scale optimization challenges.

title: # Bush Dog Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Bush Dog Algorithm" (BDA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the bush dog (Canis limbatus). The algorithm leverages the bush dog's adaptive movement strategy – characterized by short-range exploration and long-range exploitation – to navigate complex optimization landscapes. BDA employs a unique representation of the search space, a dynamic particle system with adaptive velocity and acceleration, and a novel convergence criterion based on the bush dog's tendency to settle near promising food sources. The algorithm is demonstrated on a variety of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function, showcasing its effectiveness and competitiveness compared to established metaheuristic methods such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The performance is evaluated based on convergence rate, solution quality, and computational efficiency. The results suggest that BDA is a promising approach for tackling challenging optimization problems across various domains.

title: 基于量子自旋的拓扑拓扑参数优化
abstract: Quantum spin dynamics offer a unique approach to parameter optimization, particularly in complex systems like topology. This paper investigates a novel optimization method based on quantum spin dynamics, leveraging the inherent quantum properties of spin to guide parameter adjustments within a topological structure. We propose a framework utilizing quantum spin states to iteratively refine the topological parameters, thereby enhancing the performance of quantum computation. The core mechanism revolves around a dynamic feedback loop that exploits the interplay between quantum spin states and topological structure evolution. This approach offers a promising pathway towards more efficient and robust quantum algorithms.

title: Information-Theoretic Validation of Neural Network Generalization
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to evaluating the generalization ability of neural networks using information-theoretic principles. Traditional methods often rely on empirical accuracy metrics, which can be misleading and lack a rigorous theoretical foundation. We propose quantifying information loss during the prediction process, leveraging concepts like mutual information and Kolmogorov complexity to establish a more precise and quantifiable measure of generalization. The core claim is that neural network generalization can be rigorously assessed by examining the discrepancy between the training data distribution and the distribution of predictions. This approach offers a deeper understanding of how networks learn and generalize, moving beyond simply measuring performance on a held-out dataset. The methodology provides a framework for comparing different architectures and training strategies based on their information-theoretic properties, potentially leading to improved generalization performance.

title: ## Bornean Smooth-tailed Treeshrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSTTA)
abstract: This paper introduces the Bornean Smooth-tailed Treeshrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSTTA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bornean Smooth-tailed Treeshrew (Rheophila brevicauda). The Treeshrew's unique ability to efficiently locate food sources in complex and dynamic environments serves as the core inspiration for BSTTA's design. We detail the algorithm's key components, including the exploration and exploitation phases, the adaptive parameter control mechanism, and the novel "Trail Marking" strategy. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the core principles. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in solving complex optimization tasks. The results show that BSTTA exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). Furthermore, we analyze the algorithm's sensitivity to parameter settings and discuss future research directions.

title: Dungeons That Build Themselves: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Procedural Content Generation in Roguelikes in the context of Game Development. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of PCG and roguelikes as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Game Development.

title: Algorithmic Non-Euclidean Reasoning
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of algorithmic non-Euclidean reasoning as a novel approach to tackle complex, multi-dimensional reasoning tasks beyond the limitations of traditional symbolic AI. We propose a framework that translates complex problems into non-Euclidean spaces, utilizing geometric reasoning to guide the reasoning process. The core claim is that this algorithmic approach offers the possibility of surpassing symbolic AI in handling intricate, spatially-oriented problems. This work explores the fundamental principles of this paradigm, detailing its potential advantages and challenges.
