title: Geometric Proofs of Parallel Algorithms - Automatic Verification
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to automated verification of parallel algorithms, leveraging geometric analysis to establish correctness. We introduce a system that maps parallel execution to geometric structures, allowing for the verification of properties such as convergence and optimality through rigorous geometric proofs. The core mechanism focuses on developing a mapping function that transforms the computational steps into a geometric representation, enabling automated verification using established geometric techniques. The system demonstrates the effectiveness of this approach in verifying several key parallel algorithms, showcasing significant speedups compared to manual verification methods.

title: Quantum-Driven Optimization of Parameter Space for Neural Network Architecture
abstract: Quantum-driven optimization of parameter space for neural network architecture seeks to enhance model performance through automated exploration of the network's structure. This paper presents a novel approach utilizing quantum annealing to efficiently search the parameter space of neural networks, identifying configurations with superior performance. The core mechanism leverages quantum annealing's ability to escape local optima and navigate complex landscapes, resulting in improved model accuracy and generalization. The research demonstrates the potential of this technique to significantly boost neural network capabilities.

title: A RESIDUE-DEFINED BINARY [137, 124, 2] CODE: WEIGHT SPECTRUM, COORDINATE STRUCTURE, AND AN EXACT CLASSIFICATION OF ITS MACHINE-GENERATED REALIZATIONS
abstract: We study a binary linear code C ⊆ F1372 defined by a parity-check matrix whoserows are built from residue classes modulo 15 and modulo 5 on the coordinate set {0, . . . , 136}.The construction is a member of a family generated by a four-rule machine whose inputsare subsets of the five residue types modulo 5. All results are exact integer statements overfinite spaces, verified exhaustively by machine. Main results: (i) C is a [137, 124, 2] even codewhose first eight weight moments coincide exactly with those of the binomial distribution onits 136 live coordinates; its dual C⊥ is a [137, 13] code with a unique coordinate of weight 1(a “dead coordinate”), and its full dual weight distribution is computed — 42 distinct weights,all ≡ 0, 1, 2 (mod 9), with populations 2048 : 4096 : 2048 = 2048(1 + y)2; (ii) among all 215machine inputs, exactly 24 produce a row set passing the structural package (rank 13 and aprescribed column-equivalence anatomy (28, 18, 9 × 10, 1)), and all 24 row sets are bases of thesame dual subspace: the machine selects one code, not one basis; (iii) over the free space oflinearly independent bases of the dual with the prescribed generator-weight multiset, exactly1 980 000 = 45 × 80 × 550 bases realize the target anatomy, and the shortest dependency |c| = 4of the dead coordinate is attained by exactly 2 520 = 45 × 56 of them, all of a rigidly describedform; (iv) the nine residue variants of the construction form a sunflower: pairwise intersectionsof dimension 12, common kernel of dimension 5, and the variants isospectral to the constructedcode are exactly the three residues ≡ 1 (mod 5); (v) sweeping all 504 single-site variants yieldsexactly 39 realizations with the target anatomy, all pairwise isomorphic as abstract codes —an explicit coordinate permutation is exhibited and verified for each — and exactly one ofthe 39 places the anatomy’s singleton on the distinguished “extra” coordinate 136 with theexcluded residue equal to that coordinate’s residue class, a selection possible only because137 ≡ 2 (mod 15). The code family arose in a physics-motivated combinatorial framework(the GF(2) charge structure of one Standard-Model generation); the paper is self-containedmathematics and no use is made of that origin in any proof.

title: Privacy-Preserving and Fair Training for Federated GNN
abstract: Graph neural networks (GNNs) have become a dominant paradigm for learning over graph-structured data. To protect data privacy in distributed graph settings, federated GNNs have emerged as a promising solution by enabling collaborative model training without raw data sharing. However, recent studies demonstrate that federated GNNs can inherit and even amplify biases from distributed data, resulting in unfair global models. While state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches have introduced fairness-aware federated GNN frameworks, they overlook the privacy risks arising from client–server communications during training. To address this gap, we propose SaFeGNN, a Secure and Fair Federated Graph Neural Network framework that jointly enforces privacy protection and fairness guarantees. SaFeGNN secures the communication process via additive secret sharing and client-level differential privacy, achieving stronger security guarantees compared to existing solutions. Experimental results show that SaFeGNN maintains performance close to that of the baseline, with only an additional overhead of 2.7 s and 3.6 MB per global round.

title: Anomaly Detection in Surveillance Video: An Unsupervised Unity Encoder Approach
abstract: Abstract Video anomaly detection in crowded environments is a critical task in surveillance systems to ensure public safety. Traditional approaches relying on handcrafted features, statistical models and even traditional deep learning models often struggle with the complexity of real-world scenarios. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a unique encoder-decoder based anomaly detection framework that incorporates skip connections to preserve spatial features during reconstruction and Tanh activation in the bottleneck for a balanced latent space. The approach uses a Reconstruction Error that combines Mean Squared Error (MSE) and Standard Deviation (SD) to improve sensitivity to fine anomalies. The proposed framework is evaluated on benchmark datasets i.e. UCSD Ped1, Ped2, Avenue and Shanghai. It achieved a superior performance with higher AUC and reduced Equal Error Rate (EER) thus demonstrating its effectiveness in detecting anomalies in complex environments.

title: A platform for the navigation of Unmanned Aerial Vehiclesbased on Reinforcement Learning
abstract: This article introduces a platform for developing use cases for the automated control of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), utilising the AirSim simulator. This platform allows for the generation of realistic flight scenarios involving multiple UAVs.The proposed platform facilitates the construction of use cases for the development, validation, and verification of reinforcement learning (RL) and neural networks in critical real-time systems. These algorithms can learn to navigate dynamic environments without human intervention. The platform was validated using two UAVs with neural networks that were trained using the Soft Actor-Critical (SAC) algorithm.

title: An Adaptive Hybrid Cryptographic Framework for Secure and Energy-Efficient IoT Systems: Architecture and Evaluation
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) has become a fundamental component of modern cyber–physical systems; however, securing IoT deployments remains challenging due to strict constraints on computation, memory, and energy resources. Conventional cryptographic mechanisms provide strong security guarantees but often introduce excessive overhead for low-power embedded devices, whereas lightweight cryptographic solutions may reduce security robustness under dynamic operating conditions. This paper presents an adaptive hybrid cryptographic framework for secure and energyefficient IoT systems. The proposed framework combines lightweight cryptographic primitives, hybrid key establishment, and machine-learning-assisted context-aware security selection within a unified adaptive architecture. Cryptographic configurations are dynamically selected according to runtime resource availability, data sensitivity, and inferred threat conditions while preserving bounded adaptation overhead and lightweight deployment characteristics. Experimental evaluation across representative 8-bit, 16-bit, and 32-bit IoT platforms demonstrates that the proposed framework reduces energy consumption and execution latency by approximately 15–25% compared with static cryptographic configurations while maintaining strong security guarantees and improved operational scalability. Additional adversarial validation further demonstrates resistance against downgrade manipulation, replayed context signals, oscillation-triggering attacks, and unauthorized reconfiguration attempts. The results indicate that adaptive hybrid cryptographic selection provides a practical balance between security robustness, runtime efficiency, and deployment scalability for heterogeneous IoT environments.

title: Using cyclic $$(f,\sigma )$$-codes over finite chain rings to construct $$\mathbb {Z}_p$$- and $$\mathbb {F}_q[\![t]\!]$$-lattices
abstract: Abstract We construct $$\mathbb {Z}_p$$ Z p -lattices and $$\mathbb {F}_q[\![t]\!]$$ F q [ [ t ] ] -lattices from cyclic $$(f,\sigma )$$ ( f , σ ) -codes over finite chain rings, employing quotients of natural nonassociative orders and principal left ideals in carefully chosen and not necessarily associative algebras. This approach generalizes the classical Construction A that obtains $$\mathbb {Z}$$ Z -lattices from linear codes over finite fields or commutative rings to the nonassociative setting. We mostly use (associative or nonassociative) cyclic algebras that are defined over field extensions of p -adic fields. This means we focus on certain skew constacyclic codes over finite rings to obtain $$\mathbb {Z}_p$$ Z p -lattices, hence $$\mathbb {Z}_p$$ Z p -lattice codes. title: Artificial intelligence‐assisted histopathological diagnosis of endocervical gastric‐type adenocarcinoma: a multicenter model development and validation study
abstract: Abstract Endocervical gastric‐type adenocarcinoma (GAS) is one of the most aggressive subtypes of cervical cancer and is frequently underdiagnosed due to morphological ambiguity, leading to delayed diagnosis. Despite the availability of molecular and genomic assays, their high cost, complexity, and limited reproducibility restrict clinical use. This study therefore proposes a highly sensitive artificial intelligence (AI)–assisted diagnostic system for GAS based exclusively on H&E‐stained histopathological images. We included 309 slides from 96 GAS cases collected at Peking University Third Hospital from January 2018 to January 2025, representing the largest GAS cohort reported to date for AI research. In addition, we incorporated other morphologically analogous diseases, encompassing a total of 1,320 slides sourced from four categories: normal cervical mucosa (NORM), benign endocervical lesion entities (BELE), HPV‐associated adenocarcinoma (HPVA), and endometrioid carcinoma with mucinous differentiation (ECMD). We developed GASPath, based on a novel multiple instance learning framework that efficiently captures fine‐grained morphological variations from H&E‐stained images. Beyond internal validation, GASPath was evaluated across 12 independent retrospective cohorts and further subjected to large‐scale real‐world validation on more than 7,000 samples from March 2024 to April 2025. Across three stages, GASPath demonstrated high performance. In internal validation (Stage I), it achieved an accuracy of 0.980 (95% CI 0.977–0.983) and an ROC‐AUC of 0.995 (95% CI 0.994–0.997). In external validation (Stage II), the sensitivity reached 0.902 and improved to 0.968 with proposed strategies. For biopsy samples, GASPath achieved an ROC‐AUC of 0.990 (95% CI 0.984–0.997). In large‐scale real‐world deployment (Stage III, n = 7,056), GASPath achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.953, with 100% sensitivity for GAS (45/45 cases correctly identified). The heatmaps highlight morphological features of GAS that are easily underestimated, such as irregular, angulated glands, subtle loss of nuclear polarity, and mild cytologic atypia, which show substantial morphological overlap with other diagnostic categories. GASPath enables high‐sensitivity detection of GAS in routine H&E‐stained slides, obviating the need for extensive auxiliary testing while preventing underdiagnosis and misdiagnosis. This advancement addresses a critical gap by streamlining diagnostic workflows without compromising accuracy. Its implementation could enable cost‐effective, scalable AI‐assisted diagnostics, potentially transforming the early detection and management of this aggressive cancer subtype.

title: Cross-Model Distillation of a Human-Pose Foundation Model from Unannotated Infant Video for Markerless 3D Pose Estimation
abstract: Spontaneous movement is one of the earliest windows onto an infant's neuromotor health, and structured clinical instruments that score it are validated early predictors of cerebral-palsy risk. However, they require specially trained raters, are time-consuming, and carry inter-rater variability. This motivates automated, video-based markerless assessment, especially as marker-based motion capture is impractical in infants. Yet the foundation models that make markerless capture possible are trained almost entirely on adults: our recent multi-view infant study found that no single model is jointly best, with strong 2D keypoint accuracy and direct 3D body recovery split across different models. While that study identifies this trade-off, it does not resolve it. Here, we perform cross-model distillation from the Sapiens 2 pose model into the SAM 3D Body model, using unannotated infant video alone. A frozen teacher supplies dense pseudo-labels, and a differentiable renderer aligns the predicted mesh to them in the training loop. On eleven held-out infants (18 sessions, 173 recordings) under our prior study's multi-view protocol, fine-tuning improves same-view 2D keypoint agreement with the Sapiens reference (median body percentage of correct keypoints @ 10px 0.22 -> 0.42, face 0.22 -> 0.42) and Procrustes-aligned mean per joint 3D position error (25.5 -> 22.2 mm). This demonstrates how cross-model distillation improves SAM 3D Body model performance on infants.

title: From Language to Behavior: Scaling Sequence Transformers for Industrial Recommendation Ranking with Rec-Native Designs
abstract: Scaling Transformers has driven large gains in language modeling, but transplanting this to behavior-sequence modeling in production ranking is challenging: recommendation differs in signal quality, where behavior sequences are noisy, temporally irregular, and sparsely supervised, and in computation asymmetry, where each request scores many candidates against one shared user history under tight latency budgets. We propose ReST, a recommendation-native Transformer scaling framework. For signal quality, it introduces a sequence encoder with dual-gated attention, rotary positional and temporal embedding, stabilized residual normalization, and training-only auxiliary objectives. For computation asymmetry, it factorizes ranking into a heavy reusable encoder and a lightweight cross decoder with projection-free KV attention and token-specific parameterization, coupling user-level shared-prefix training with shared-prefix serving for compute-once, decode-many-times ranking. Across industrial and public benchmarks, ReST achieves higher accuracy and scales more consistently along sequence length, depth, and width, where LLM-style Transformer blocks saturate. A one-week online A/B test on a production advertising platform improves online AUC by 1.31% and lifts a core revenue metric by 11.93% within a 50 ms P99 budget; ReST has since been fully deployed in production, showing that behavior-sequence scaling remains a promising, under-exploited axis for production ranking.

title: The Fermionic Cohomology Problem on the Full Fock Space Is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-Complete
abstract: Fermionic cohomology detects zero-energy states of supersymmetric Hamiltonians. Previous work showed that deciding nonzero cohomology in an input-specified particle-number sector is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-hard and belongs to $\mathrm{QMA}$. We study total cohomology on the unrestricted full Fock space, where a NO instance must exclude zero-energy states in every sector and in their superpositions. We prove that this global problem is $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-complete. The input differential is an operator that raises fermion number by one and squares to zero on the full Fock space. It is given as an exact list of local fermionic monomials, each involving at most $41$ modes. The reduction encodes each data site by one fermion in a block of modes. Every sector violating this occupation rule has energy at least one. An exact quantum verifier accepts a suitable witness with certainty on every YES instance, establishing containment with perfect completeness. We also prove $\mathrm{QMA}_1$-completeness for the problem in an input-specified particle-number sector. Its hard instances use $30$-mode terms and admit a one-dimensional block-chain realization.

title: Soft-Argmax for the Projective Plane via the Veronese Embedding
abstract: From horizon detection to fibre structures in X-ray imaging, many vision tasks recover lines via peak detection in Hough space $H=S^1\times\mathbb{R}$, the domain of orientation-offset pairs $(θ,ρ)$. Differentiable pipelines extract coordinates via \emph{soft-argmax}, a probability-weighted average that is only meaningful in a globally linear space. However, $(θ,ρ)$ and $(θ+π,-ρ)$ describe the same undirected line, so $H$ double-covers the space of undirected lines $H/\mathbb{Z}_2$: a Möbius strip, obtained by identifying each pair under $\mathbb{Z}_2$ action. Soft-argmax operates on the cover $H$, but since $H/\mathbb{Z}_2$ admits no linear structure, it tears geometrically adjacent lines apart. Thus we need a $\mathbb{Z}_2$-invariant embedding of lines into a linear space, on which soft-argmax is well-defined. We achieve this by parametrising lines via unit-norm homogeneous vectors $\ell=(1+ρ^2)^{-1/2}(\cosθ,\sinθ,-ρ)^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^3$ and applying the Veronese map $v_2(\ell)=\ell\ell^{\top}$ that satisfies $v_2(\ell)=v_2(-\ell)$. This descends continuously to an embedding of the quotient $H/\mathbb{Z}_2$ into the linear space $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, where the antipodal ambiguity vanishes. Line extraction becomes a barycentre in $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\mathbb{R}^3)$, projected back via its leading eigenvector. We validate our \emph{Veronese soft-argmax} in a Hough transform-based network across all resolvable lines, confirming uniform and seam-free recovery. We further derive that the $L_2$-loss on isometrically weighted Veronese embeddings equals the squared chordal distance between lines in projective space, enabling a geometrically precise training objective.

title: A No-Defense Defense Against Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on ML-NIDS: Is Less More?
abstract: Gradient-based adversarial attacks subtly manipulate inputs of Machine Learning (ML) models to induce incorrect predictions. This paper investigates whether careful architectural choices alone can yield an inherently robust Deep Neural Network (DNN)-based Network Intrusion Detection Systems (NIDS), without any additional explicit defenses. Through thousands of experiments, around 2200, varying network depth, feature dimensionality, activation functions, and dropout across FGSM, PGD, and BIM attacks, we show that shallower networks, reduced feature sets, and ReLU activation consistently and jointly reduce adversarial vulnerability. Moreover, a simple model following this recipe outperforms deeper, fully-featured adversarially trained models, while maintaining near-perfect clean-traffic detection and lower training times. Nevertheless, while less is more, the selection of the right less is what truly matters.

title: Racialized Hate Speech in YouTube Comments on The Little Mermaid (2023): A Critical Discourse Analysis
abstract: This study examined the manifestation and linguistic construction of racialized hate speech in YouTube comments responding to Disney’s 2023 live-action adaptation of The Little Mermaid. The casting of a Black actress as Ariel generated polarized reactions, making the trailer comment section a productive site for examining digital hostility as a discursive practice. Using qualitative content analysis informed by Mondal’s (2017) typology of hate speech and critical discourse analysis drawing on Van Dijk’s (2006) socio-cognitive approach, the study analyzed selected comments drawn from a larger corpus of approximately 78,000 comments containing discriminatory indicators. The findings reveal three primary manifestations of racialized hostility: race-based, behavior-based, and physical-based expressions. However, these categories frequently overlap and interact through recurring linguistic patterns rather than appearing as isolated forms. Hostility is often articulated through modal constructions, evaluative adjectives, negation, and semantic prosody that position racial representation as a deviation from an imagined cultural norm. Rather than relying on explicit slurs, many comments employ coded and indirect forms of antagonism that allow speakers to express exclusionary attitudes while maintaining plausible deniability. The study demonstrates how racialized hate speech operates as discursive resistance to perceived transformation of cultural norms in participatory media environments. By foregrounding the linguistic mechanisms underlying online hostility, this research contributes to applied linguistics and digital discourse studies by revealing how YouTube's algorithmically mediated environment amplifies subtle racialized hostility, while offering a framework for anti-racism education, digital literacy initiatives, and platform content moderation.

title: Can LLMs Explain AI? A Study of Explainable AI in Cybersecurity Machine Learning Models
abstract: This work evaluates whether Large Language Models (LLMs) can support Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) in cybersecurity, as standalone tools or combined with SHAP and LIME. Experiments with Random Forests on three intrusion detection datasets compared GPT-5 and GPT-OSS-20B explanations to SHAP and LIME. Standalone LLMs showed semantic bias and hallucinated feature importance, while SHAP/LIME-grounded prompts improved faithfulness and coherence. In a qualitative study on explainability in cybersecurity with 38 participants, LLM+SHAP/LIME explanations were preferred over SHAP/LIME-only. GPT-5 achieved the highest preference, while GPT-OSS-20B demonstrated the potential of lightweight local LLMs for XAI.

title: Seismological Reconstruction of Meteoroids: Trajectories, Physical Parameters, and Strewn Fields in Wind-Perturbed Atmospheres
abstract: Every day, the Earth's atmosphere is struck by meteoroids, and the recovery of fresh meteorite material is the main way of improving our understanding of how the Solar System and the Earth formed. However, meteorite recovery is often limited because not all meteorite-producing meteoroids are observed. Meteoroid detection is currently dominated by optical fireball networks, whose individual cameras are affected by clouds, daylight and spatial coverage gaps. Dense, globally distributed seismic networks offer a time- and weather-independent alternative. Since meteoroids continuously generate acoustic waves during their supersonic flight, the resulting air-to-ground coupled seismic waves can be used to reconstruct their atmospheric path. This provides a distinct physical method of constraining meteoroid parameters. However, exploiting this approach requires a new framework to systematically detect meteoroid signals in seismic data and reconstruct trajectories in wind-perturbed atmospheres. Only then can the seismic method reliably complement the current approaches to estimating meteoroid parameters, trajectories, and meteorite ground locations. In this work, we outline the development and application of this end-to-end framework, which covers meteoroid detection to meteorite strewn-field reconstruction. First, we compile the Seismo-Acoustic Meteoroid Observation Recording Database (SMORD), which contains 307 meteoroid events and 3,295 manually labelled arrivals across a global set of stations. We then use this database to train a PhaseNet-based deep-learning phase picker in SeisBench. The model achieves 91% precision and 94% recall (AUC 0.89), with a median absolute timing error of 0.02 s. We demonstrate how this model can automatically detect meteoroid onsets and reconstruct the trajectory of a meteoroid over the Adriatic Sea. We then improve the trajectory reconstruction method by using the uncontrolled re-entry of the Starlink-2382 satellite as a meteoroid equivalent. By incorporating a 3D wind model and a lift-like parameter into a ray-based direct-search optimisation, we significantly improve the travel-time fit to recording data from 226 stations. This allows us to recover an entry velocity of $8.9 \pm 0.7$ km s$^{-1}$ and an effective ablation coefficient consistent with near-complete ablation of the ${\sim}100$ kg main satellite fragment. Using collocated acoustic and seismic sensors, we found that the acoustic-to-seismic ground coupling coefficients vary by up to three orders of magnitude (from $4.31 \times 10^{-10}$ m s$^{-1}$ Pa$^{-1}$ to $5.86 \times 10^{-7}$ m s$^{-1}$ Pa$^{-1}$), mainly due to differences in near-surface rock stiffness. Finally, we use probabilistic Markov chain Monte Carlo ensemble sampling to perform a statistically robust reconstruction of the 8 March 2026 Koblenz meteoroid trajectory, which was recorded at 95 stations. Replacing direct ray computation with a precomputed lookup table reduces new ray calculations to simple interpolation, enabling this full Bayesian inversion of the meteoroid trajectory. With this trajectory and the associated uncertainties that can be propagated, we recover the heliocentric orbit and initial mass of 305 +180/-90 kg of the meteoroid. Additionally, we identify five distinct fragmentation events along the atmospheric trajectory and calculate a strewn field, which is validated against fragments that struck a building in Koblenz-Güls. Together, these results demonstrate the successful application of the end-to-end acoustic-seismic framework which can shape future meteoroid trajectory reconstructions and enables the rapid, automated calculation of meteorite strewn fields.

title: betwixt: Scoped Semantic Claims and Human Review Workflows
abstract: Betwixt is a lightweight framework for constructing, representing, and reviewing candidate semantic claims in tabular data. It provides a pragmatic review layer in which candidate knowledge can be organised into bounded review tasks and presented for human judgement. Betwixt keeps candidate semantic structure separate from its presentation for review. Candidate data can be projected into human-reviewable forms, while review decisions, states, and provenance remain explicit and reproducible.

title: How Missingness Mechanism and Imputation Strategy Jointly Shape the Stability of Post-Hoc Feature Attributions: A Cross-Model Empirical Study
abstract: Post-hoc feature-attribution methods such as SHAP and permutation importance are widely used to explain the predictions of machine learning models trained on tabular data, yet real-world tabular datasets are rarely complete: values go missing according to different underlying mechanisms, and practitioners routinely impute them before scoring or explaining a model. Prior work has shown that the choice of imputation method can bias SHAP values, but this line of work has generally examined a single missingness mechanism and a single attribution method in isolation. It remains unclear whether the mechanism generating the missingness (Missing Completely at Random, MCAR; Missing at Random, MAR; or Missing Not at Random, MNAR) interacts with the choice of imputation strategy, whether such effects are consistent across model families, and whether different attribution methods (SHAP versus permutation importance) reach the same practical conclusions about which imputation strategy is safest. We address these questions with a controlled empirical study on two public tabular benchmarks (the Breast Cancer Wisconsin diagnostic dataset and the Pima Indians Diabetes dataset), amputing held-out test data under all three missingness mechanisms at three missing-data rates (10%, 20%, 30%), imputing with three established strategies (mean/median, k-nearest-neighbours, and iterative/MICE-style imputation), and re-scoring three frozen model families (logistic regression, random forest, and LightGBM) trained on the complete data. We measure attribution stability as the Spearman rank correlation between the SHAP or permutation-importance ranking obtained under each imputed scenario and the ranking obtained on the complete-data oracle test set, using 978 experimental conditions with repeated random masking and non-parametric statistical testing (Friedman, Wilcoxon signed-rank with Holm correction, Kendall's tau, and bootstrap confidence intervals). We find that (i) missingness mechanism has a statistically significant but numerically small effect on SHAP stability, with MNAR producing significantly lower stability than MCAR (Holmcorrected p = 0.0042); (ii) imputation method has a large and highly significant effect (Friedman chisquare = 52.4, p = 4.1e-12), with mean/median imputation producing markedly less stable SHAP rankings than KNN or iterative imputation, but this effect is concentrated almost entirely in LightGBM and is negligible for logistic regression; (iii) SHAP-based rankings are dramatically more stable under imputation than permutation-importance rankings (median Spearman correlation approximately 1.00 versus 0.90, with permutation importance showing a long tail of near-zero correlations); and (iv) SHAPbased and permutation-based attribution methods agree on which imputation strategy is best for explanation stability in only 33% of dataset-model-mechanism combinations (mean Kendall's tau = 0.15), meaning that the practical recommendation a practitioner would derive depends on which attribution method they use to evaluate it. These results suggest that explanation-stability audits under missing data should be attribution-method-specific and model-family-specific rather than treated as a single generic property of a dataset, and that permutation importance in particular should be interpreted cautiously whenever the scored features have been imputed.

title: Quantum Error Correction Memory Unit
abstract: This paper presents the design and theoretical framework for a single-bit quantum error correction memory unit based on the principles of quantum error correction. The core claim is to construct a fault-tolerant memory unit for storing quantum information reliably. The proposed unit utilizes a multi-party quantum error correction coding scheme coupled with an error decoding system to mitigate the effects of decoherence and noise on individual qubits. The key innovation lies in the efficient implementation of quantum error correction at the single-qubit level, addressing a critical bottleneck in quantum computing. The theoretical framework details the encoding and decoding processes, emphasizing the real-time feedback mechanism for sustained quantum state preservation. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the operation of the unit, including the error correction codes and the decoding algorithms. The unit's design offers a pathway toward scalable quantum memory solutions, crucial for advanced quantum computation and quantum communication protocols.

The key innovation lies in the efficient implementation of quantum error correction at the single-qubit level, addressing a critical bottleneck in quantum computing. The theoretical framework details the encoding and decoding processes, emphasizing the real-time feedback mechanism for sustained quantum state preservation. Mathematical formulations are presented to illustrate the operation of the unit, including the error correction codes and the decoding algorithms. The unit's design offers a pathway toward scalable quantum memory solutions, crucial for advanced quantum computation and quantum communication protocols.

title: Quantum Machine Learning in Adaptive Attention Mechanisms
abstract: Quantum Machine Learning (QML) is a rapidly developing field that explores the potential of quantum computers to enhance machine learning algorithms. A critical challenge in QML is the design of efficient and effective attention mechanisms, which are fundamental to many deep learning architectures, particularly in natural language processing and computer vision. This paper investigates the application of adaptive attention mechanisms within the context of QML, specifically focusing on the design of a novel self-adaptive attention mechanism leveraging quantum properties. We propose a framework that dynamically adjusts the attention weights based on the quantum state, allowing for a more nuanced and efficient modeling process. The core claim is that this design will result in improved model performance and enhanced learning efficiency compared to traditional attention mechanisms, utilizing the inherent advantages of quantum computing. This work presents a theoretical analysis and preliminary implementation of this novel approach.

title: Decentralized Verification of Federated Learning Models
abstract: Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a promising paradigm for training machine learning models on decentralized data sources without direct data sharing. However, ensuring the integrity and accuracy of these models remains a significant challenge. Traditional verification methods often rely on centralized aggregation, inherently compromising user privacy and introducing a single point of failure. This paper proposes a novel blockchain-based system for decentralized verification of FL models. The system leverages cryptographic proofs, specifically zero-knowledge Succinct Non-Interactive Argument of Knowledge (zk-SNARKs), allowing nodes to independently verify model updates without revealing the underlying data. This approach eliminates centralized aggregation, enhancing privacy and establishing a verifiable, distributed ledger of model updates. The core claim is that current decentralized verification methods are computationally expensive and rely on centralized aggregation, thus, this system offers a truly decentralized and privacy-preserving verification framework.

title: Caspian Seal Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSMA)
abstract: This paper presents the Caspian Seal Metaheuristic Algorithm (CSMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the behavior of Caspian seals during their foraging activities. The algorithm incorporates key aspects of seal hunting strategies, including exploratory movement, targeted searching, and adaptive adjustment based on environmental feedback. CSMA utilizes a population-based approach with a dynamic representation of the search space, employing a 'seal' concept to simulate individual foraging agents. The core components of CSMA include a 'seal density' parameter controlling exploration, a 'seal targeting' mechanism for focused searching, and an 'adaptive adjustment' function reflecting environmental changes. The algorithm's performance is evaluated through simulations on various benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. Mathematical formulations for key aspects of the algorithm, such as the probability of seal movement and the adjustment factor, are detailed. The results indicate that CSMA exhibits robust convergence properties and competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like Genetic Algorithm and Particle Swarm Optimization. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Artificial Intelligence, Foraging Behavior, Seal, Novel Algorithm.

title: Quantum Topology Information Encoding: An Adaptive Geometric Mapping Algorithm
abstract: Quantum topology information encoding provides a powerful framework for representing and manipulating complex geometric structures, offering unprecedented capabilities for numerical simulations. This paper introduces a novel algorithm, termed "Adaptive Geometric Mapping," that leverages quantum entanglement to achieve precise modeling and computation of intricate geometric forms. The core mechanism centers around a dynamically adjusted mapping process guided by quantum entanglement, significantly enhancing the accuracy and efficiency of numerical simulations. We propose a method for generating and manipulating geometric representations using entangled qubits, enabling the resolution of problems previously intractable for classical methods. The proposed algorithm demonstrates significant improvements in the simulation of topological structures, particularly in the context of quantum field theory and geometric analysis. Furthermore, the paper discusses the theoretical underpinnings of the adaptive mapping process and outlines future research directions, including exploring the potential for scaling this approach to larger, more complex geometries.

title: Dynamic Adaptive Random Matrix Optimization
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic adaptive random matrix optimization method designed to enhance the stability and robustness of parameter optimization processes. Traditional parameter optimization methods often fail to fully leverage the inherent properties of the problem matrix, leading to suboptimal solutions. This work proposes a method that dynamically adjusts the random matrix structure during the optimization process, effectively capturing and exploiting these structural characteristics. The core mechanism involves iteratively modifying the random matrix to guide the search towards optimal parameter values, mitigating the sensitivity to initial parameter choices. We present a rigorous theoretical analysis and demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through extensive experiments on a range of optimization problems. The results demonstrate a significant improvement in optimization stability and convergence speed compared to existing methods.

title: Title: Quantum State Collapse Optimization (QSCO)
abstract: Quantum state collapse is a fundamental process in quantum mechanics, and its optimization represents a significant challenge in quantum information processing. This paper introduces Quantum State Collapse Optimization (QSCO), a novel optimization technique designed to enhance fidelity collapses by explicitly modeling decoherence dynamics and employing a Bayesian approach to estimate collapse probabilities. The core mechanism of QSCO involves dynamically adjusting collapse parameters based on observed decoherence, while also incorporating a 'quantum memory' to preserve critical information. We demonstrate QSCO's effectiveness through simulations and analysis, showcasing a significant improvement in fidelity compared to existing collapse algorithms. This research addresses limitations in current approaches, particularly concerning the handling of complex decoherence patterns and the potential for achieving higher fidelity collapses.

title: Quantum Entanglement Multi-Dimensional Geometry Analysis
abstract: Quantum entanglement, traditionally viewed as a correlation between particles, possesses the potential to manifest within complex geometric structures in higher dimensions. This research explores the possibility that entanglement may form intricate geometric tensors, allowing for precise definition and computation of its properties, potentially unveiling novel quantum information processing algorithms. We introduce a novel quantum entanglement model based on multi-dimensional geometry, leveraging non-local quantum information theory to construct a dynamically evolving geometric tensor, and develop algorithms to precisely analyze entanglement's geometric characteristics. This work represents a significant departure from conventional quantum computation by focusing on the geometric properties of entanglement, offering a new perspective on its potential for manipulation and analysis.

title: Title: Non-Linear Boltzmann Machines for Complex Dynamical Systems
abstract: Abstract: The investigation of complex dynamical systems presents a significant challenge in various fields, including physics, biology, and engineering. Traditional approaches often rely on simplified models, failing to capture the intricate relationships governing these systems. This paper explores the application of Non-Linear Boltzmann Machines (NLBMs) as a novel framework for modeling such systems, focusing on the ability to exhibit emergent behavior. We propose a new architecture incorporating feedback loops and non-linear dynamics within the Boltzmann Machine, designed to facilitate the development of complex and unpredictable behavior. The core mechanism involves a carefully designed network of interconnected nodes and connections, allowing for the propagation of information through the system. This approach has the potential to significantly advance our understanding and modeling capabilities for dynamic systems exhibiting complex, non-linear patterns. The study will detail the theoretical groundwork, architecture, and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the capacity of this new approach to generate novel dynamical behaviors. The focus will be on the inherent limitations of standard Boltzmann Machine implementations in handling such complexity.

title: Title: Universal Simulation of Complex Fluid Dynamics via Quantum Field Theory
abstract: This paper explores the potential of quantum field theory (QFT) to revolutionize the simulation of complex fluid dynamics, offering a pathway to significantly enhanced computational power and the capture of emergent behaviors previously unattainable through conventional methods. We introduce a novel framework predicated on quantum entanglement to model fluid particle dynamics, aiming to overcome the computational bottlenecks inherent in traditional fluid simulations. The core claim is to develop a QFT-based simulation system capable of handling increasingly complex fluid phenomena with unprecedented fidelity. The paper details the proposed methodology, outlining the mathematical foundations and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the framework's potential. We emphasize the role of quantum entanglement as a key enabling principle for achieving this transformative approach.

title: Mammography AI Agent: integración de modelos mamográficos preentrenados mediante votación blanda ponderada
abstract: Prototipo de investigación desarrollado para una tesis de la Maestría en Dirección de Tecnologías de la Información de la Universidad ESAN. Integra tres modelos mamográficos preentrenados (GMIC, DMV-CNN/NYU y GLAM) en un agente único mediante votación blanda ponderada, sin entrenar ninguna red nueva. El repositorio contiene la arquitectura de orquestación, los adaptadores de conjuntos de datos, el procedimiento de selección de configuración con validación cruzada estratificada, la interfaz demostrativa y los artefactos de la evaluación formal. No es un dispositivo médico. No ha sido validado clínicamente ni cuenta con autorización regulatoria. Los modelos preentrenados no se redistribuyen: se descargan de sus repositorios oficiales durante la construcción de las imágenes, bajo los términos de New York University. Tampoco se redistribuye ninguna imagen médica. Véase el archivo NOTICE.

title: A Conceptual Architecture for AI-Driven Adaptive Apprenticeship and Lifelong Career Learning
abstract: In a rapidly changing job market, professional value can no longer rely solely on initial education, making continuous learning essential for career sustainability. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), mobile technologies, and ubiquitous connectivity enable personalized and context-aware learning experiences that support lifelong learning. This article proposes a conceptual adaptive learning model for career development that integrates learners' objectives, knowledge levels, learning styles, and contextual information to guide personalized learning pathways. Through AI-driven adaptation of content and difficulty, the model illustrates how learner engagement, motivation, and knowledge retention can be enhanced. Positioned within workplace learning environments, the proposed model supports continuous upskilling and reskilling. The paper presents the model's design principles and explores future opportunities such as predictive career path modeling, multimodal adaptation, and context- and emotion-aware learning, while emphasizing ethical and collaborative considerations.

title: Deep Learning as a Projection Method for Solving Economic Models
abstract: Deep learning is increasingly presented in economics as a new paradigm for solving dynamic models, superseding the classical projection methods of numerical economics.We argue that this dichotomy rests on a misclassification.The neural-network solvers emphasized in this literature are least-squares projection methods with an adaptive nonlinear parameterization.Placing deep learning inside the projection family reorients the agenda.The issue is not a contest between paradigms, but suggests a single toolkit using a variety of approximation methods, residual criteria, and evaluation designs to be chosen on the merits for the model at hand.In low and moderate dimensions, linear-basis and sparsegrid methods are often more accurate, faster, and easier to verify than a trained neural network.In high dimensions, an appropriate choice for the space of permissible functions will often avoid the curse of dimensionality.

title: depictr: A Unified Toolkit for Visualising Statistical Models and Data
abstract: A cohesive, publication-ready toolkit of plots that span the whole analysis workflow with one consistent look.It covers exploratory data analysis (distributions, categorical summaries, bivariate plots, scatter-plot matrices, correlation heatmaps, missing-data maps, outliers, estimation statistics and descriptive tables); multivariate analysis, clustering with diagnostics and Kaplan-Meier survival curves; time series (trends, autocorrelation, decomposition, seasonality and forecasting); model estimates and inference (forest plots, model comparison, frequentist and Bayesian estimates, predicted values, interactions, random effects and optimiser checks); diagnostics and classification (residual panels, binned residuals, influence, quantile-quantile, receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves, calibration, threshold tuning and confusion matrices); uncertainty and power; and reporting helpers (a shared theme, colourblind-aware palettes, plot composition and saving).Every plotting function returns a 'ggplot2' object (or a 'patchwork' object for composite panels), heavier modelling back-ends are optional, and the package ships with reproducibly simulated datasets so that every example and vignette runs without further setup.

title: Digital Transformation in Pathology: A Digital‐First Model for Integrated Diagnostic Systems
abstract: Digital pathology has rapidly expanded over the past decade, driven by advances in whole-slide imaging and increasing demand for remote and data-integrated diagnostic workflows. However, many implementations remain limited to partial digitization, without fundamentally transforming laboratory and diagnostic processes. In this review, we examine digital transformation in pathology as a systems-level redesign encompassing workflow optimization, digital infrastructure, and networked diagnostic services. Using the implementation at International University of Health and Welfare (IUHW) Narita Hospital as an illustrative example, we describe how a digital-first approach can be integrated into routine clinical practice. Key elements include continuous laboratory workflows aligned with slide digitization, comprehensive digital infrastructure enabling seamless access to diagnostic data, and networked systems that support multi-institutional collaboration and subspecialty consultation. We further discuss how digital pathology extends beyond clinical diagnosis to support education and research, transforming traditional slide archives into accessible data resources, and outline practical considerations for implementation, including workflow redesign, user adoption, and institutional coordination. Finally, by comparing the IUHW Narita experience with other large-scale implementations, we discuss generalizable principles for digital transformation in pathology, including workflow-driven design, data integration, interoperability, and network-based diagnostic models.

title: Development and Crossover Evaluation of an Artificial Intelligence‐Assisted System for Solid Pancreatic Lesion Detection and Pancreatic Parenchyma Recognition in Endoscopic Ultrasonography (With Video)
abstract: BACKGROUND AND STUDY AIMS: Pancreatobiliary endoscopic ultrasonography (EUS) is technically demanding, and supervised training opportunities are limited. We developed an artificial intelligence (AI) overlay system for detecting solid pancreatic lesions (SPL) and recognizing pancreatic parenchyma (PP) and evaluated its effect on reader performance. PATIENTS AND METHODS: Across six centers, two deep learning-based models were trained using expert-annotated EUS frames. We then conducted a randomized, two-sequence, two-period crossover reader study in which eight endosonographers (five novices and three experts) interpreted image sets with and without AI assistance. The primary endpoint was superiority of sensitivity for SPL detection among novices; key secondary endpoints included specificity and PP recognition. RESULTS: From 118 patients, 120 SPL-positive/negative image sets and 160 PP-positive/negative image sets were constructed. Among novices, AI assistance improved SPL detection sensitivity (88.7% vs. 76.8%, p < 0.001) and accuracy (86.4% vs. 78.7%), while specificity met the predefined noninferiority criterion (84.2% vs. 80.5%, p < 0.001). For PP recognition, sensitivity increased numerically (86.3% vs. 83.3%) but did not meet the predefined superiority criterion (p = 0.095); specificity met the noninferiority criterion (87.8% vs. 81.0%), and accuracy increased from 82.1% to 87.0%. Among experts, sensitivity was maintained for both tasks, whereas specificity increased with AI assistance. CONCLUSIONS: AI assistance improved SPL detection among novice endosonographers. For PP recognition, sensitivity increased without reaching statistical superiority, whereas specificity met the predefined noninferiority criterion. These findings support a potential adjunctive role for AI in EUS interpretation.

title: Named Entity Recognition Across Datasets and Domains: Resources and Models for Galician
abstract: Abstract Automatic named entity recognition (NER) is essential for many natural language processing applications, particularly in low-resource languages and those with corpora restricted to a single domain, where the lack of diverse data may hinder cross-domain generalisation. In this context, we attempt to contribute to the Galician NER field by extending manually annotated resources and exploring several approaches to improve the performance of automatic classifiers. To this end, we enrich two new datasets with NER annotations in Galician, which we release in this paper. Through experimental evaluation, we investigate the benefits of fine-tuning transformers on NER data by comparing various monolingual and multilingual BERT models and developing a new extra-small DeBERTa model for Galician. Furthermore, we assess the quality of the NER model by expanding the initial training corpus with additional data from related varieties, including Portuguese and Spanish. For evaluation, we use five Galician corpora, including our two newly annotated datasets and three adapted from existing resources, ensuring assessment across multiple domains. Our findings reveal (1) a positive impact of enhanced cross-lingual training data on improved model performance across five Galician test datasets; (2) similar performance of monolingual and multilingual models depending on the training data; and (3) the competitive effectiveness of extra-small BERT models for Galician NER tasks compared to larger models.

title: An Implant-to-Wearable IR-UWB Transmitter-Receiver Architecture and Layered Protocol for High-Density Brain-Computer Interfaces
abstract: High-rate neural telemetry requires an implant-towearable link whose circuit partition, waveform mapping, packet processing, and failure semantics are mutually consistent. This paper specifies a chip-oriented, one-way impulse-radio ultrawideband (IR-UWB) uplink comprising an implanted packet engine and free-running transmitter, a tissue-proxy channel, and a wearable mixed-signal receiver and digital baseband.

title: From classical to quantum reinforcement learning and its applications in quantum control: A beginner’s tutorial
abstract: This tutorial is designed to make reinforcement learning (RL) more accessible to undergraduate students and researchers by offering clear, example-driven explanations. It focuses on bridging the gap between RL theory and practical coding, addressing common challenges that one faces when transitioning from conceptual understanding to implementation. Through hands-on examples and approachable explanations, the tutorial aims to equip the reader with the foundational skills needed to confidently apply RL techniques in real-world scenarios. title: KOMPARASI KINERJA CONVNEXT DAN CONVNEXTV2 UNTUK KLASIFIKASI CITRA ENDOSKOPI GASTROINTESTINAL MENGGUNAKAN DATASET HYPERKVASIR
abstract: Identifikasi dini lesi gastrointestinal (GI) sangat penting untuk mencegah perkembangan polip menjadi kanker kolorektal. Namun, evaluasi manual citra endoskopi oleh ahli medis bersifat subjektif dan rentan terhadap kesalahan klasifikasi akibat tingginya kesamaan visual antar-jaringan. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk membangun dan membandingkan performa model deep learning murni berbasis konvolusi, yaitu ConvNeXt-tiny dan ConvNeXtV2-tiny, dalam melakukan klasifikasi citra endoskopi gastrointestinal. Dataset yang digunakan diperoleh dari situs resmi HyperKvasir pada kelompok labeled-images yang disaring menjadi 12 kelas berbeda. Guna mengatasi ketimpangan data, diterapkan teknik class balancing undersampling sehingga setiap kelas memiliki jumlah data yang seragam, yaitu 391 citra. Dataset dibagi dengan rasio 70% data pelatihan, 20% data validasi, and 10% data pengujian. Teknik augmentasi data berupa rotasi, pembalikan vertikal/horizontal, dan random crop diaplikasikan pada data pelatihan hingga jumlahnya meningkat tiga kali lipat. Kedua model dilatih dengan konfigurasi hyperparameter yang sama, meliputi batch size 16, optimizer SGD, fungsi loss CrossEntropyLoss, learning rate 0,0001, dan durasi pelatihan 30 epoch. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa model ConvNeXtV2-tiny berhasil meminimalkan overfitting dan mengungguli model pendahulunya dengan mencapai akurasi data uji sebesar 96,04%, nilai macro average precision 96,08%, recall 96,04%, F1-score 96,05%, serta skor ROC-AUC mencapai 99,85%. Sebaliknya, model ConvNeXt-tiny mengalami overfitting yang ditandai dengan fluktuasi grafik loss validasi dan hanya memperoleh akurasi pengujian sebesar 92,71% serta ROC-AUC 99,45%. Model ConvNeXtV2-tiny dengan performa terbaik selanjutnya diimplementasikan ke dalam aplikasi web menggunakan Streamlit untuk pengujian klasifikasi secara langsung. Penelitian ini membuktikan bahwa integrasi fitur Global Response Normalization (GRN) dan kerangka kerja Fully Convolutional Masked Autoencoder (FCMAE) pada ConvNeXtV2 secara signifikan meningkatkan kemampuan generalisasi model dalam mengenali pola visual medis yang kompleks. Kata kunci: Gastrointestinal, Klasifikasi citra endoskopi, Deep Learning, ConvNeXtV2, Dataset HyperKvasir.

title: SKTRC: Rastreamento Direcionado e Persistente de Eventos do Kernel Linux para Análise de Vulnerabilidades
abstract: Vulnerabilities in Linux Kernel components may involve internal states that are difficult to observe and transient events that are relevant for security analysis. Although there are well-established tracing mechanisms, these approaches do not always combine targeted collection, contextualization, persistence, and low instrumentation effort. This work introduces the Simple Kernel Trace (SKTRC), a Kernel module aimed at targeted and persistent tracing of internal system events. SKTRC was evaluated in a Proof of Concept (PoC) executed on a native bare metal Linux installation and compared with the native event tracing mechanism. The evaluation used components associated with the Copy Fail vulnerability, which was recently disclosed after remaining present for years in the Linux Kernel. The results indicate that SKTRC makes it possible to collect contextualized logs during the controlled execution of a vulnerability PoC, reduces the instrumentation effort, and facilitates subsequent analysis of security-relevant events.

title: Looking Things Up Before Speaking: A Critical Survey Review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of RAG and retrieval as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: 基于量子纠错码的分布式算法容错性分析
abstract: This paper investigates the resilience of distributed algorithms against errors, a critical challenge in quantum computing and networked systems. We propose a novel approach to analyzing the fault tolerance of distributed algorithms by leveraging the principles of quantum error-correcting codes (QECCs). Specifically, we develop a framework for quantifying the error correction capabilities of QECCs in the context of distributed algorithms, considering factors such as code distance, decoding efficiency, and network topology. Our analysis provides a rigorous method for evaluating and optimizing distributed algorithms for enhanced reliability. The core of our work lies in translating the theoretical properties of QECCs into practical metrics for assessing algorithmic robustness, and we present a methodology for guiding algorithm design based on these metrics. The results of our analysis demonstrate the potential to significantly improve the resilience of distributed algorithms through strategic code selection and network configuration. We aim to provide a foundational understanding for designing fault-tolerant distributed systems utilizing quantum technologies.

title: Dynamic Plasticity Machine Learning
abstract: Dynamic Plasticity Machine Learning (DPML) is a novel machine learning framework that introduces a dynamic plasticity mechanism to model parameters. This mechanism allows the model parameters to adapt based on the input data, thereby enhancing the model's generalization ability and adaptability. This approach contrasts with traditional static parameter adjustment methods, offering a more responsive and robust learning process. This paper explores the design of this dynamic plasticity framework, detailing its implementation, performance evaluation, and potential applications in various machine learning domains.

title: 基于非线性几何的量子纠缠模拟算法
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, exhibiting correlations between distant particles that cannot be explained by classical physics. Accurate simulation of entangled states is crucial for various applications, including quantum computing and quantum cryptography. Traditional quantum state simulation relies heavily on particle systems, which often struggle to represent the intricate nature of entangled states. This paper introduces a novel algorithm based on non-linear geometry, aiming to significantly improve the accuracy and efficiency of quantum entanglement simulation. We propose a geometric framework that visualizes entanglement as a set of non-linear curves and surfaces, allowing for more precise representation and accelerated computation. The core mechanism involves mapping the quantum state onto a non-linear geometry, enabling enhanced entanglement dynamics. This research advances the field by providing a new approach to quantum entanglement simulation that surpasses the limitations of traditional methods, opening up possibilities for more robust and efficient quantum computation.

title: Buff-footed Antechinus: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by its Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Buff-footed Antechinus Optimization" (BAO), inspired by the foraging behavior of the *Antechinus stulti* (Buff-footed Antechinus). This small marsupial exhibits remarkable efficiency in locating and exploiting food resources in a patchy environment. BAO mimics this strategy through a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance, incorporating elements of both stochastic and deterministic search techniques. The algorithm utilizes a population of potential solutions, represented as vectors, and iteratively refines these solutions based on a 'patch quality' assessment and a 'movement probability' influenced by the current solution's fitness and the overall population's performance. The core of BAO lies in a novel 'patch selection' mechanism that dynamically adjusts the probability of moving to new patches, weighted by the estimated potential benefit. Mathematical formulations of the algorithm's key components, including patch quality evaluation and movement probability calculation, are provided. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in achieving high solution quality and robustness. The results indicate that BAO provides a competitive alternative to established metaheuristic methods, particularly in problems exhibiting patch-like characteristics or requiring a balance between exploration and exploitation.

title: Decentralized Machine Learning via Byzantine Fault Tolerance Graph Networks
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to decentralized machine learning (DML) that leverages graph networks and Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) mechanisms to achieve robust and reliable learning outcomes, even when confronted with malicious actors. The core idea is to construct a specialized graph network where nodes collaboratively learn while simultaneously detecting and mitigating Byzantine attacks. This architecture fundamentally addresses the critical security concerns inherent in DML systems. We introduce a framework where nodes communicate via message passing, utilizing a dedicated mechanism for identifying and isolating compromised nodes. The integrity of the learning process is maintained through a BFT protocol integrated within the graph network. The resulting system exhibits resilience against various attack vectors, ensuring the accuracy and consistency of the learned models. Mathematical formulations detail the key components of the system, including the network topology, the learning algorithm, and the BFT protocol. We demonstrate the theoretical benefits of this approach and outline a potential implementation strategy. Our research contributes to the growing field of secure and trustworthy DML, paving the way for applications in domains demanding high levels of resilience, such as autonomous vehicles, IoT networks, and distributed sensor systems.

title: Brush Rabbit: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Brush Rabbit Behavior
abstract: This paper presents Brush Rabbit, a newly developed metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of brush rabbits. The algorithm leverages the rabbit's efficient movement pattern and resource exploitation strategies to achieve robust optimization performance. Brush Rabbit incorporates a novel adaptive parameter control mechanism, termed "Brush Velocity," which dynamically adjusts the search speed based on the local landscape gradient and the historical information of the best solution. The algorithm utilizes a population-based approach, employing a swarm of rabbits, each represented by a position and velocity vector. The objective function is minimized through iterative movement and resource selection. The performance of Brush Rabbit is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its competitive capability compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC). The key features of Brush Rabbit include: (1) Adaptive Brush Velocity control, (2) Probabilistic resource selection, and (3) Dynamic swarm density management. The results indicate that Brush Rabbit is a promising alternative for tackling complex optimization challenges.

title: Brandt's Ground Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Foraging Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Brandt's Ground Squirrel, a novel metaheuristic algorithm designed to address complex optimization problems. The algorithm is inspired by the foraging behavior of Brandt's ground squirrels, specifically their strategies for efficiently locating and exploiting food resources. Brandt's Ground Squirrel combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) algorithms, introducing a dynamic territory assignment mechanism and a probabilistic exploration phase. The core innovation lies in the algorithm's ability to adaptively adjust the size and distribution of territories, mimicking the squirrels' shifting search areas based on resource availability. Mathematical formulations detailing the territory assignment, resource evaluation, and probabilistic exploration are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on several benchmark functions, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Key performance indicators, including convergence rate and solution quality, are analyzed. Future research directions focusing on parameter tuning and integration with other optimization techniques are discussed.

title: Boto: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Behavior of the Boto Bird
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, Boto, inspired by the foraging behavior of the Boto bird (also known as the Japanese Tit). Boto leverages the Boto's unique ability to efficiently locate food sources in a patchy environment by incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation. The algorithm utilizes a modified version of the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) framework, integrating a "patch-seeking" mechanism and a dynamic adjustment of individual velocities based on local patch density. The performance of Boto is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness and competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The core mathematical formulation of Boto is presented, along with detailed explanations of its key components and parameters. The algorithm's ability to adaptively balance exploration and exploitation is a key feature, leading to improved convergence rates and solution quality. Future research directions include exploring the algorithm's suitability for different problem domains and investigating its potential integration with other optimization techniques.

title: Bornean Short-tailed Gymnure Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSG-MHA)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, the Bornean Short-tailed Gymnure Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (BSG-MHA), motivated by the foraging behavior of the Bornean Short-tailed Gymnure (Crossarchus tanganale). The algorithm leverages key aspects of the gymnure's movement strategy – specifically its opportunistic exploration, risk-averse decision-making, and adaptability to changing environments – to design a robust optimization process. BSG-MHA incorporates a novel exploration strategy based on a 'scatter-and-seek' mechanism mimicking the gymnure's search pattern, and a modified adaptive inertia weight scheme inspired by the animal's cautious approach to food sources. The algorithm employs a dynamic population size and a stochastic local search component to enhance its convergence rate and solution quality. We evaluate BSG-MHA on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms such as Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The results indicate that BSG-MHA's design, rooted in the observed behaviors of the Bornean Short-tailed Gymnure, offers a promising approach to tackling complex optimization problems.

title: Quantum Computing Optimization Algorithms: A Novel Approach Based on Topological Structures
abstract: Quantum computing offers unparalleled computational power, but its practical implementation is hindered by the complexities of quantum algorithms. Traditional optimization methods often struggle to effectively leverage the unique quantum properties, limiting overall performance. This paper proposes a novel quantum algorithm optimization approach, leveraging topological structures to refine quantum parameter configurations, ultimately driving enhanced efficiency and accuracy in quantum computation. We present a theoretical framework and preliminary experimental results demonstrating the efficacy of this methodology.

title: Bolivian Bamboo Rat Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Bamboo Rat Optimization Algorithm" (BROA), inspired by the foraging behavior of the Bolivian Bamboo Rat. The algorithm leverages the rat's efficient exploration and exploitation strategies in a complex environment to solve various optimization problems. BROA incorporates key characteristics of the rat's behavior, including its use of scent marking, movement patterns, and resource prioritization, into a mathematical framework. The core of the algorithm revolves around a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) technique with a novel adaptive inertia weight and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. We present a detailed description of the BROA algorithm, including its key parameters and operational rules. Furthermore, we demonstrate the algorithm's effectiveness on a range of benchmark optimization problems, including the Rosenbrock function, the Rastrigin function, and the Sphere function. The results show that BROA performs competitively with established metaheuristic algorithms such as PSO and Genetic Algorithm (GA) in terms of convergence speed and solution quality. Finally, we discuss potential future research directions and extensions of the BROA algorithm.

title: Black-tailed Dasyure Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by Black-tailed Dasyure Behavior
abstract: This paper presents the Black-tailed Dasyure Algorithm (BTDA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of the black-tailed dasyure ( *Sminthopsis leuis* ). Dasysures are known for their efficient and adaptive foraging strategies in complex environments. BTDA leverages these strategies through a combination of particle movement, memory preservation, and adaptive parameter adjustment. The algorithm utilizes a black-tailed dasyure's movement pattern – primarily foraging along edges of a search space – to guide the optimization process. The core components of BTDA include a position update rule influenced by the gradient of the objective function and a memory mechanism that retains promising solutions. Adaptive parameters, namely the inertia weight (w) and the cognitive and social coefficients (α and β), are dynamically adjusted based on the algorithm's performance. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions. The key performance metrics include convergence speed, solution quality, and computational complexity. This research provides a valuable contribution to the field of metaheuristic optimization by introducing a biologically inspired algorithm with promising performance characteristics.

title: Sarcoma Region of Interest (ROI) Images - Part 6
abstract: Bone and soft tissue (BST) tumors are a heterogeneous and rare group of mesenchymal neoplasms that pose significant diagnostic challenges owing to their complex morphologies and overlapping histological features. Despite rapid advances in digital pathology, most publicly available datasets predominantly focus on common epithelial tumors and offer a limited representation of BST tumors. To address this gap, we introduced the Pathologist-Annotated Image Retrieval dataset for Bone and Soft Tissue tumors (PAIR-BST), a dataset consisting of 2,252 pathologist-annotated regions of interest derived from 470 whole slide images obtained from 268 patients diagnosed with BST tumors. Each region was curated and annotated with multi-level labels, including 33 histologic diagnoses, 11 lines of differentiation, and 6 growth patterns, enabling comprehensive characterization of the morphological heterogeneity inherent to BST tumors. Benchmark experiments have demonstrated that pathology foundation models face challenges in identifying these tumors, particularly when distinguishing between tumor subtypes and growth patterns. PAIR-BST offers a high-quality, discriminative benchmark for the development and evaluation of pathology foundation models, specifically focusing on rare mesenchymal tumors.[Metadata Availability] Additional metadata containing specific coordinates for all ROIs (Regions of Interest) within the WSI, along with labels such as diagnosis for each, is available in a separate .csv file at: https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.33383509 (also linked in the related materials below). Find related datasets in the collection at https://doi.org/10.25452/figshare.plus.c.8223469

title: Introduction to this special section: Machine learning
abstract: Machine learning has emerged as one of the most consequential forces shaping the next chapter of geoscience, moving swiftly from a promising research frontier to an increasingly practical part of the geoscientist’s toolkit. As geoscience data sets continue to expand in size, variety, and complexity, the need for methods that can recognize subtle patterns, accelerate interpretation, predict subsurface properties, and support timely decisions has become ever more pressing. Machine learning offers a powerful response to this challenge. It can help classify geologic patterns, delineate structural features, forecast reservoir behavior, and extract meaningful information from data that would be difficult to examine fully by conventional means alone. Equally important, it invites geoscientists to revisit familiar workflows through the lens of automation, reproducibility, and efficiency.

title: Leveraging LLM Embeddings for Ontology Scope Optimisation and Reuse in Construction Transportation Data Integration to Enhance Construction Logistics
abstract: Abstract Just-in-Time is a key lean construction principle aimed at reducing time, costs, and onsite emissions, but it increases reliance on precisely timed logistics. Integrating construction logistics with traffic and mobility data is currently hindered by fragmented open data sources and a lack of shared semantics. This paper investigates the use of large language model (LLM) embeddings to support ontology engineering for external mobility data that must be aligned with Just-in-Time construction logistics requirements. We propose a semi-automated workflow that uses embeddings to cluster domain terms, analyse ontology scope, identify relevant open data offers from a national mobility data platform, and suggest candidates for ontology reuse. We approach ontology scope optimization as a systematic refinement process driven by semantic embeddings. The scope of the ontology is to provide a structured representation of external datasets and their linkage points to internal concepts, rather than modeling the internal domain itself. A manually crafted baseline ontology serves as the reference for these mappings, and LLM-embedding-supported insights provide guidance. The results show that embedding-based methods can uncover missing concepts, improve concept alignment, and highlight reusable ontology fragments. At the same time, polysemy and unstable LLM outputs underline the need for systematic quality assurance.

title: Refined monogamy and polygamy relations for multipartite quantum entanglement
abstract: Abstract Monogamy and polygamy relations quantify complementary restrictions on the distribution of entanglement in multipartite quantum systems. We establish two endpoint-matched scalar inequalities that retain a hierarchy-dependent mixed term discarded by standard weighted estimates. Conditional on a valid base-power monogamy or polygamy relation for the chosen entanglement quantity and state class, these inequalities yield refined tripartite bounds and recursive extensions to arbitrary numbers of parties. Analytical comparison with earlier coefficients proves that the resulting monogamy lower bounds are no smaller and the polygamy upper bounds are no larger throughout the common parameter domain. Concurrence and concurrence-of-assistance examples verify the ordering and identify the equality conditions.
