title: MutMem-V2: Cryptographically Authorized Mutation in Persistent Agent Memory Portable Verification and Reproducible Evidence
abstract: MutMem V1 introduced retention-preserving, cryptographically authorized mutation for persistent agent memory but did not provide a complete portable verification contract or clean-install reproduction path. MutMem V2 closes that publication gap without introducing a second memory engine. It specifies exact canonical bytes, domain-separated object and bundle commitments, mandatory recall-evidence membership and ordering, external trust anchors, identity epochs, revocation, authorization, request receipts, ordered disclosure, and three mutation terminal types. The released protocol contains 18 versioned object schemas, 39 recall vectors, 15 mutation vectors, and 37 closed recall failure reasons. Independent Node and Python implementations agree on verdict and primary reason for all 72 structural and cryptographic terminals; a production-conformance corpus agrees on 42/42 cases across 28 required classes. A clean Node v26.8.1 installation reaches first-boot, restart, and scheduler readiness with no experimental memories. A separately scoped 120-unit Canary experiment supports only explicit-marker traversal. Every public table regenerates from a self-hashed aggregate, and an independent verifier reconstructs the statistics and claim boundaries. Historical V1 empirical results remain historical. MutMem V2 supports claims about portable integrity, authorization, traceability, conformance, and reproducibility under stated assumptions; it does not establish semantic truth, universal robustness, or independent replication.

title: CRSF: Collusion-Resilient Privacy-Preserving Sensor Fusion with Byzantine-Robust Participation
abstract: Privacy-preserving sensor fusion enables an untrusted server to compute an aggregate result over distributed sensor measurements without learning either individual inputs or the final output. Recent garbled-circuit-based protocols provide an efficient realization of this functionality in a sensor--server--client architecture, but remain vulnerable to sensor--server collusion and Byzantine manipulation of sensor participation. These weaknesses can compromise honest-sensor privacy, incorrectly exclude honest sensors, and corrupt the computed fusion result, thereby undermining the security guarantees expected from the protocol. We present CRSF, a collusion-resilient sensor-fusion protocol that addresses these weaknesses while providing privacy, correctness with explicit abort, and liveness. CRSF introduces a Practical Byzantine Fault Tolerance (PBFT)-based agreement phase for sensor submissions and uses server-specific, status-dependent label release with threshold protection of circuit-input labels. This design prevents any Byzantine server from unilaterally manipulating sensor participation and prevents any admissible sensor-server coalition from obtaining enough secret material to compromise honest-sensor privacy. We implement CRSF and compare its online execution time with the most relevant state-of-the-art baseline. Our Google Cloud evaluation measures the total computation and communication cost of the online protocol under fault-free and representative faulty executions. Across a range of fault-tolerant fusion circuits and up to 261 sensors, CRSF demonstrates a highly practical trade-off between robust security and protocol performance.

title: Photonic fusion operations transform partial distinguishability
abstract: Photonic fusion operations are a central primitive in photonic quantum information processing and are commonly characterized by their success probability and resource cost. Here, we identify an additional way in which different implementations of fusion operations differ, namely in how they transform partial distinguishability. We consider distinguishability originating both from imperfect entangled resource states and from imperfect single photons. We find that different successful fusion events can induce markedly different distinguishability transformations depending on the fusion protocol, heralding outcome, and error model. Under a collective resource-state error model, we identify a modification to an existing fusion protocol that improves the fidelity of the remaining state on average. Generally, however, these transformations adversely affect distinguishability, and many successful fusion outcomes are accompanied by distinguishability degradation. Our results show that partial distinguishability is dynamically shaped by interference and measurements and should be considered alongside overall fusion success probability when evaluating photonic fusion protocols.

title: Learning Task-Specific Antibody Representations via Function-Aware Masking
abstract: Antibody-specific language models pretrained via masked language modeling (MLM) learn representations that are critical for downstream sequence design and property prediction tasks. Yet, the corruption process itself is rarely leveraged as a source of inductive bias during pretraining. While preferentially masking complementarity-determining regions (CDRs) improves binding-related predictions, antibodies possess diverse biological priors over a variety of functions. Herein, we introduce function-aware masking, a family of pretraining algorithms that align mask placement with specific functional priors (e.g., from IMGT annotations or structure predictions) to shape the learned representation space. We show that these specialist masking strategies significantly improve performance on their respective objectives, yielding up to a 14% gain on structure-related tasks and up to a 5.9x improvement on CDR-related tasks. To further improve performance across multiple functional axes, we develop hybrid masking strategies that integrate multiple priors, balancing reconstruction over binding, structural, and biophysical objectives. Our results demonstrate that informed mask placement provides a parameter-free mechanism for imposing functional inductive biases in antibody language model training.

title: ESTIMASI POTENSI PEMBANGKITAN DAYA MATAHARI DARI PANEL SURYA UNTUK PERANCANGAN PLTS ATAP DI KOTA BENGKULU
abstract: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis potensi pembangkitan energi listrik dari panel surya untuk perancangan PLTS atap di Kota Bengkulu. Data yang digunakan terdiri dari data radiasi matahari NASA POWER periode Januari sampai Desember 2025 serta data pengukuran langsung menggunakan pyranometer berbasis Internet of things (IoT) selama 25 hari. Data NASA POWER meliputi kondisi all sky dan clear sky, sedangkan data pyranometer digunakan sebagai pembanding lapangan. Hasil pengolahan data NASA POWER menunjukkan bahwa radiasi matahari kondisi clear sky berada pada kisaran 454–548 W/m², sedangkan kondisi all sky berada pada kisaran 334–374 W/m². Nilai clear sky index berkisar antara 0,619– 0,772 dan cloud loss sebesar 22%–38%. Estimasi energi listrik PLTS pada kondisi all sky berada pada rentang 2,908–5,964 kWh/kWp/hari, sedangkan kondisi clear sky sebesar 6,756–7,289 kWh/kWp/hari. Hasil pengukuran pyranometer menghasilkan rata-rata energi spesifik sebesar 4,35 kWh/kWp/hari, mendekati rata�rata NASA POWER all sky sebesar 4,45 kWh/kWp/hari. Dengan demikian, Kota Bengkulu memiliki potensi yang baik untuk pengembangan PLTS atap. Kata kunci: radiasi matahari, PLTS atap, NASA POWER, pyranometer, energi surya.

title: evermore Differentiable Binned Likelihood Functions with JAX
abstract: Statistical analyses in high energy physics often rely on likelihood functions of binned data. These likelihood functions can then be used for the calculation of test statistics in order to perform statistical inference over parameters of physics interest. evermore is a Python package for building and evaluating these likelihood functions using JAX - a powerful Python library for high performance numerical computing. The key concepts of evermore are computational performance and differentiability. JAX provides automatic differen- tiation, just-in-time (JIT) compilation, and vectorization capabilities, which can be leveraged to improve the performance of statistical analyses. JIT-compilation and vectorization can be used for parallelizing fits on GPUs which is especially advantageous for likelihood scans and estimation of toy based upper limits. We present the concepts of evermore, show its features, and give concrete examples of its computational performance in the context of a CMS analysis.

title: Policy-Constrained Runtime Defense for Tool-Using AI Agents in Enterprise API Ecosystems
abstract: Tool-using AI agents can invoke internal APIs, retrieve documents, update records, and coordinate enterprise workflows. These capabilities create a runtime security problem: an agent may select an unauthorized tool, hallucinate an endpoint, follow malicious instructions embedded in retrieved context, rely on poisoned memory, retry unsafe operations, or submit a schema-valid but policy-violating payload. This paper presents a policy-constrained runtime enforcement framework that intercepts each proposed action before execution and classifies it as allow, deny, or escalate. We implement a deterministic trace-driven simulator with five service domains, six user roles, six threat classes, benign and adversarial tasks, and four defense configurations. The evaluation isolates enforcement effectiveness by replaying identical seeded action traces across all configurations. Across 8,000 controlled workflow executions, the framework reduces adversarial attack success from 100.0% for an unconstrained agent, 72.2% for prompt-only controls, and 18.5% for static gateway rules to 0.2%. It achieves a 99.9% overall safe-outcome rate, 100.0% benign safe completion under simulated reviewer approval, a 4.8% benign false-positive rate, and a 24.9 ms median enforcement latency. Ablation results show that registry validation, authorization, retry governance, and intent checking directly reduce attack success. Payload inspection addresses schema-valid semantic misuse, while context-integrity and escalation controls provide defense-in-depth and operational-governance benefits. The framework provides a structured basis for controlled evaluation of policy-constrained runtime enforcement across tool-using enterprise agents.

title: Algoritmo para Detecção e Mitigação de Ataques de Inversão de Rótulos no Aprendizado Federado
abstract: O Aprendizado Federado (FL) permite treinar modelos de aprendizado de máquina de forma distribuída, preservando a privacidade dos dados. No entanto, ataques como o label-flipping podem comprometer o desempenho do modelo global. Este artigo tem como objetivo principal avaliar os impactos desse ataque em cenários com privacidade diferencial (DP) e compactação de modelos baseada em FedSketch, além de desenvolver e avaliar um método de detecção de clientes mal-intencionados para aumentar a robustez do treinamento.

title: Multimodal Artificial Intelligence for Breast Cancer Detection Using Medical Imaging and Clinical Data
abstract: Breast cancer diagnosis typically involves both medical images and clinical text reports, but many existing AI systems analyze only one type of data at a time.This makes it difficult to connect information from scans and clinical notes, which can limit diagnostic accuracy.In this paper, we propose an AI-based multimodal framework for breast cancer detection that integrates both imaging data and textual information.The system supports text-only input, image-only input, or both, which are processed using separate encoders and combined through a fusion mechanism.By learning a shared representation of these data types, the proposed approach improves breast cancer classification, tumor localization, and clinical decision support, making the results more accurate and reliable.

title: 基于量子纠缠的自适应图神经网络
abstract: This paper introduces a novel neural network architecture, termed a Quantum Entanglement-Aware Graph Neural Network (QEA-GNN), which leverages the principles of quantum entanglement to enhance the training process of graph neural networks. The QEA-GNN utilizes entanglement to dynamically adjust the network's parameters, leading to improved model performance and faster convergence. We explore the potential of this approach by demonstrating its effectiveness in a series of benchmark datasets. The core mechanism focuses on establishing entangled representations between nodes, allowing the network to learn more robust and informative features. The paper presents a detailed analysis of the algorithm's design, implementation, and performance evaluation. We conclude that the QEA-GNN offers a promising avenue for advancing graph neural network training through the incorporation of quantum entanglement.

title: Topological Redundancy in Quantum Entanglement Encoding
abstract: This paper investigates the potential of incorporating topological redundancy into quantum entanglement encoding schemes. The core claim is that strategically designing quantum entanglement codes leveraging specific topological structures can significantly enhance the resilience of quantum entanglement, ultimately leading to more efficient quantum information transmission. This approach utilizes the topological protection effect, shielding entangled states from local perturbations by encoding them within the inherent topology of the system. Furthermore, topological redundancy allows for the reconstruction of complex entanglement networks using a limited number of entangled pairs. The theoretical framework presented here outlines the key principles and potential benefits of this novel approach, offering a pathway towards robust and scalable quantum technologies. We explore the mathematical underpinnings of this strategy, focusing on the encoding and decoding processes within the defined topological framework. The central equation governing the entanglement fidelity is: F = |⟨ψ|Φ⟩|2 where ψ represents the encoded state and Φ represents the measured state. The topological protection ensures that small perturbations will not significantly alter the state |ψ⟩, thus maintaining a high fidelity. The concept of topological redundancy is formalized as: R = Σi |ψi⟩⟨ψi| where ψi are the fundamental entangled states and R describes the overall redundant information. This redundancy allows for the reconstruction of more complex entangled states through appropriate combinations of the fundamental states. This work provides a foundational understanding for future research into topological quantum information processing.

title: 基于自适应的语言学习的语法规则生成
abstract: This paper introduces a novel approach to grammar rule generation based on adaptive learning, aiming to automate the refinement of grammatical rules and produce more consistent and linguistically-appropriate rules. The core of this method lies in the implementation of a self-adaptive model that continuously adjusts grammar rules based on the characteristics of input text. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of experiments evaluating its ability to generate grammatically sound and contextually relevant rules across a diverse range of linguistic data. The resulting system offers a promising step towards automated grammar development, potentially reducing the need for manual intervention and accelerating the process of creating high-quality language models. The proposed method provides a framework for creating more robust and adaptable grammar rules, capable of handling the complexities of natural language.

title: Cambodian Striped Squirrel: A Novel Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of *Turdus rex*
abstract: This paper introduces the Cambodian Striped Squirrel (CSS) algorithm, a new metaheuristic optimization technique inspired by the foraging behavior of the Cambodian Striped Squirrel (*Turdus rex*). The algorithm mimics the squirrel's strategic movement patterns, incorporating elements of exploration and exploitation to effectively navigate complex search spaces. CSS utilizes a novel representation of the search space based on a grid, simulating the squirrel's territory. Movement decisions are governed by a stochastic rule set, influenced by the squirrel's observed habits of alternating between focused searching and broader exploratory sweeps. The algorithm employs a dynamic territory adjustment mechanism, mirroring the squirrel's adaptation to resource availability. We demonstrate the efficacy of CSS through theoretical analysis and simulations, showcasing its performance across a range of benchmark optimization problems. The results demonstrate CSS's capability to converge quickly and effectively, achieving competitive results compared to established metaheuristic methods. The core innovation lies in the combined use of a grid-based representation, stochastic movement rules, and dynamic territory management, resulting in a robust and adaptable optimization strategy.

title: California Pocket Gopher Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CPGIMA)
abstract: This paper introduces the California Pocket Gopher Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm (CPGIMA), a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm designed to address complex problems with non-linear and multi-modal landscapes. The algorithm draws inspiration from the burrowing behavior of the California pocket gopher, specifically its exploration strategy and adaptation mechanisms. CPGIMA utilizes a modified particle swarm optimization (PSO) framework with a dynamically adjusted velocity and position update scheme, mimicking the gopher's ability to adapt its tunneling path based on local terrain and environmental factors. The core innovation lies in the 'Terrain Awareness' component, which simulates the gopher's sensitivity to soil composition and moisture levels, influencing the movement direction and speed of particles. We present the algorithm's theoretical foundations, detailing the key parameters and their impact on performance. The performance of CPGIMA is evaluated through a series of benchmark problems, demonstrating its effectiveness compared to established metaheuristic algorithms like PSO and Genetic Algorithm. The results showcase CPGIMA's capability in achieving high solution quality and computational efficiency. Keywords: Metaheuristic Optimization, Particle Swarm Optimization, California Pocket Gopher, Burrowing Behavior, Terrain Awareness, Algorithm Design.

title: 自适应拓扑几何的自适应参数调整
abstract: This paper presents a novel approach to adaptive parameter adjustment within the framework of self-adaptive topology geometry. Traditional optimization algorithms often rely on fixed parameter sets, limiting their ability to adapt to complex and varying problem landscapes. This work introduces a method that dynamically adjusts the algorithm's parameters based on the underlying topology of the problem space, thereby enhancing the algorithm's ability to generalize to diverse instances. The core mechanism leverages the inherent dynamic nature of topology, enabling the algorithm to explore and refine its solution space more effectively. This results in improved performance and robustness in various optimization tasks. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through several illustrative examples, showcasing its ability to effectively adapt to changing parameters and achieve superior results compared to static optimization methods. The paper concludes with a discussion of the theoretical implications and potential future research directions.

title: Bunny Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by Rabbit and Rat Behavior
abstract: This paper introduces Bunny Rat, a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of rabbits and rats. The algorithm leverages the exploratory and exploitative tendencies observed in these animals, mimicking their movement patterns and resource selection strategies. Bunny Rat combines elements of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and Simulated Annealing (SA) within a dynamically adjusted adaptive strategy. Specifically, the algorithm employs a 'hopping' movement mechanism to explore the search space, influenced by a 'preference' factor derived from the local environment. The 'preference' factor, calculated using a weighted average of neighborhood solution fitnesses, guides the hopping direction. A 'nesting' mechanism is also incorporated, simulating the rats' tendency to establish and defend a preferred location. The algorithm's parameters, including hopping probability, preference weight, and nesting radius, are dynamically adjusted based on the convergence rate and stagnation levels. Experimental results on benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that Bunny Rat achieves competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging landscapes with complex multimodal distributions. The algorithm's performance is evaluated using metrics such as convergence speed, solution quality, and computational efficiency. Future research directions include incorporating reinforcement learning to further refine the adaptive mechanisms and exploring the algorithm's applicability to different problem domains.

title: Title: Adaptive Information Encoding (AIE)
abstract: Abstract: Adaptive Information Encoding (AIE) presents a novel method for encoding information, designed to dynamically adjust representation quality based on the context of the receiving system. This approach aims to enhance communication and learning efficiency by creating representations that are sensitive to the receiver's state. The core mechanism of AIE leverages a probabilistic encoding scheme that generates representations tailored to specific contexts, optimizing for both communication and learning effectiveness. This paper explores the design and evaluation of AIE, highlighting its advantages over existing encoding techniques.

abstract: Quantum state dynamics, a novel approach to quantum system modeling, offers the potential to achieve precise system representation and prediction by incorporating dynamic geometric transformations. The core mechanism centers around establishing a geometric deformation model, utilizing computational techniques to reveal these relationships. The study demonstrates the efficacy of this approach in enhancing the accuracy of quantum state simulations.

title: Brazilian Three-banded Armadillo Algorithm: A Novel Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm Inspired by the Behavioral Patterns of *Tolypeutes tridecemlineatus*
abstract: This paper presents the Brazilian Three-banded Armadillo Algorithm (BT3AA), a newly developed metaheuristic optimization algorithm inspired by the foraging behavior of *Tolypeutes tridecemlineatus*, the Brazilian three-banded armadillo. The algorithm leverages the armadillo's unique strategy of exploring the environment in a three-banded pattern – moving forward, circling back, and then moving forward again – to effectively search for food sources. BT3AA incorporates these behavioral elements into a novel optimization process, utilizing a population-based approach with adaptive parameters. The algorithm's core mechanics include a position update strategy mimicking the armadillo's pattern, a fitness evaluation function that reflects resource availability, and a local search component inspired by the armadillo's tactile sensing during foraging. We demonstrate the effectiveness of BT3AA through simulations and comparisons with established metaheuristic algorithms – namely, the Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) and the Artificial Bee Colony (ABC) – on several benchmark problems. The results indicate that BT3AA exhibits competitive performance, achieving optimal or near-optimal solutions in many cases, and demonstrating robustness across different problem landscapes. Future research will focus on refining the algorithm's parameters and exploring its applicability to a wider range of optimization challenges.

title: 基于机器学习的动态拓扑变形算法
abstract: This paper introduces a novel dynamic topology transformation algorithm based on machine learning. Traditional topology transformation methods often rely on manual design, limiting flexibility and requiring extensive expertise. This work proposes a machine learning-driven approach that automatically learns and generates complex topology structures, facilitating system control and optimization. The core mechanism involves training a model to predict and guide topology transformations, achieving a level of automation previously unattainable. The algorithm's novelty lies in its ability to learn complex topology directly from data, offering a significantly more adaptable and efficient solution compared to traditional methods. This research explores the potential of machine learning to automate the creation of intricate and dynamically evolving systems.

title: ## Blackish Small-eared Shrew Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed "Shrew-Inspired Metaheuristic Optimization (SIMHO)," inspired by the foraging behavior of the Blackish Small-eared Shrew ( *Soriculus ater* ). These shrews exhibit a unique strategy for locating food sources in complex and uncertain environments, characterized by intermittent rewards and significant spatial variability. SIMHO leverages this adaptive foraging strategy through a combination of probabilistic search, memory-based decision-making, and a dynamic exploration-exploitation balance. The algorithm utilizes a 'trail' representation analogous to the shrew's olfactory trail, combined with a 'memory' component mirroring the shrew's recollection of past successful locations. Mathematical formulations describing the core components of SIMHO, including the trail update mechanism, memory management, and parameter adjustment, are presented. The algorithm's performance is evaluated on a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating its effectiveness in finding near-optimal solutions within reasonable computational time. Keywords: Metaheuristic Algorithm, Optimization, Blackish Small-eared Shrew, Foraging Behavior, Trail Representation, Memory-Based Optimization, Exploration-Exploitation Balance.

title: Comment on essd-2026-244
abstract: Abstract. Proximal hyperspectral imaging has been widely used in material analysis, mineral mapping, and related geological studies. However, most publicly available datasets are limited to a single observation scenario and commonly lack corresponding mineralogical and geochemical constraints, which restricts quantitative analysis, cross-scenario comparison, and objective method evaluation. To meet this need, this study presents a multi-scenario proximal shortwave infrared imaging hyperspectral dataset for geological samples collected from typical clay-type lithium deposits hosted in carbonate successions in China, systematically covering four complementary observation scenarios, including powder, drill core, hand specimen, and in-situ outcrop. The data were acquired using a HySpex imaging spectrometer covering 960–2500 nm. In addition to the hyperspectral imagery, the dataset integrates mineralogical information, geochemical information, sampling annotations, reference panel spectra, geographic locations, and related metadata, thereby establishing a unified framework linking spectral observations, sample composition, and spatial context. For the controlled indoor scenarios, the dataset provides reflectance data, whereas for the field in-situ scenario it provides radiometrically corrected imagery together with reference panel spectra and example products for data use. The dataset is organized in standard and widely used formats. title: Unified Evaluation Benchmark for Temporal Knowledge Graph Representation Learning
authors: CHEN Yijing, LI Qian, DU Yuntao, LIU Lei, YAN Zhongmin
abstract: Temporal knowledge graph representation learning (TKGR-LE) aims to embed dynamic facts and entity relationships into a low-dimensional vector space to capture the semantic evolution along the time dimension. This technique is widely applied in various scenarios, such as financial risk control, recommender systems, and event prediction. However, despite its promising outlook, the development of this field is significantly hampered by a profound lack of standardization. Existing studies often focus exclusively on the construction and validation of a single model, resulting in a deficit of a unified, reproducible experimental framework and a set of objective, standardized evaluation protocols. This “siloed” approach severely limits the performance comparison and technical exchange among different models, greatly constraining the overall progress and rapid iteration of algorithms in this domain. To address this critical bottleneck, this paper proposes a unified framework for temporal knowledge graph representation learning. The core objective of this framework is to establish a standardized system for research, development, and evaluation. Utilizing a modular design paradigm, it standardizes the entire workflow, encompassing model design, implementation, and evaluation, and constructs an integrated experimental platform. Specifically, this paper systematically reproduces and optimizes eight categories of temporal algorithms, including TTransE and TA-DistMult. This paper conducts temporal-aware link prediction experiments on standard benchmark datasets, such as ICEWS and YAGO. Furthermore, multi-dimensional comparative experiments are performed to validate the advantages of this framework in algorithmic compatibility, evaluation objectivity, and scenario universality. This research endeavors to establish a standardized R&D and evaluation system for temporal knowledge graphs. By introducing a normalized performance comparison mechanism, it provides a crucial baseline framework to facilitate future algorithmic iteration and technological innovation.

title: The Vampire Diary
abstract: During the past years of continuous development, the Vampire theorem prover has become an automated solver for machine-based proof search in the combined theories of commonly-used data structures. Central to Vampire is saturation-based first-order theorem proving using the superposition calculus, which has by now extended to support arithmetic, induction, code synthesis, higher-order logic, proof certification, and many more. These advances have been made to meet the demands of mathematical formalization and trustworthy system development. In this talk we discuss the aforementioned advances in Vampire, overview the main changes Vampire has undergone during the past years, and survey some of the design choices we made during this process. We believe our advances in saturation-based reasoning proved to make a difference. Vampire outperforms or complements many other state-of-the-art reasoners, including leading SMT solvers and inductive theorem provers. For example, in the past two editions of the CASC world championship in theorem proving, Vampire won all competition divisions and proved more problems than any other system in every competition division. This talk is based on the joint work of the Vampire developers’ team, including Filip Bártek, Ahmed Bhayat, Jonas Bodingbauer, Robin Coutelier, Bernhard Gleiss, Márton Hajdu, Matthias Hetzenberger, Petra Hozzová, Jack McKeown, Merisa Mustajbasic, Jakob Rath, Michael Rawson, Axel Polaczek, Giles Reger, Martin Suda, Johannes Schoisswohl, Andrei Voronkov, and Eva-Maria Wagner. Our work was funded in whole or in part by the ERC Consolidator Grant ARTIST 101002685, the ERC Proof of Concept Grant LEARN 101213411, the FWF SpyCoDe Grant 10.55776/F85, the SBA Research COMET Center SBA-K1 NGC managed by the FFG, and the WWTF grant [ForSmart Grant ID: 10.47379/ICT22007].

title: Performance Analysis of a Decentralized Federated Learning System for Spoken-Command Recognition: Resilience and Security Considerations
abstract: In the industrial edge-to-cloud continuum, data is often privacy-sensitive and spans multiple organizations that do not fully trust one another, making central aggregation of raw data undesirable and often non-compliant with regulations such as the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR). Federated Learning (FL) addresses this by sharing model updates rather than raw data, but conventional FL assumes a central coordinator, leaving it exposed to poisoning and inference attacks and to a single point of trust and failure. Decentralized Federated Learning (DFL) couples FL with Distributed Ledger Technologies (DLTs), removing the coordinator and enabling verifiable aggregation in trustless, cross-organizational environments. In this work, we assess the applicability of DFL to on-device spoken-command recognition—a representative edge audio task underpinning voice-driven industrial interfaces—by comparing decentralized and centralized training under idealized and adversarial conditions. Using a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) replicated across edge nodes, we evaluate resilience to inter-node data imbalance, to poisoning attacks, and to a privacy-preserving noise-injection defense against inference attacks, together with model compression for resource-constrained edge devices. The system pairs this comparison with a validation-based poisoning defense in which each node scores its peers’ updates on its own held-out data, and an update is aggregated only if a majority of nodes report a weighted F1-score above a threshold—requiring neither a shared validation set nor a trusted validator. Our results indicate that the DFL system achieves accuracy comparable to centralized baselines in most scenarios (weighted F1-score 0.762 across nine nodes, against 0.896 centralized), and that a cross-node validation mechanism reliably excludes poisoned updates as long as fewer than half of the nodes are compromised (within 3.54% of the unpoisoned model). Noise-based inference defenses reduce accuracy substantially (44.7% on average at a noise standard deviation of 1.0), exposing a sharp privacy–utility trade-off, whereas model compression preserves performance (0.765 against 0.762 for pruning and format conversion, with 8-bit quantization costing up to a further 13.3%). These findings clarify both the promise and the current limitations of decentralized, privacy-preserving learning for the industrial edge-to-cloud continuum.

title: Sistema de toma de decisiones jerárquico para robots de servicio
abstract: The deployment of service robots in shared environments requires decision-making architectures capable of managing inte-rruptions and maintaining continuous operation. This paper presents a hierarchical control system based on Behavior Trees (BT)designed for the Sancho robotic platform. The system is structured into four priority layers: energy management, conversationalinterruptions, high-level mission execution, and passive idle routines. Through its implementation in ROS 2 and the use of ashared memory (Blackboard), the design separates decision-making from the underlying navigation, perception, and interactionmodules. Experimental evaluation in a physical environment demonstrates the platform’s responsiveness to context changes.The system allows interrupting base navigation to attend to voice commands, seamlessly integrating newly queued missions,and aborting execution in the face of critical events to ensure recharging, validating the feasibility of the design for unattendedoperation.

title: Τεχνικές καθολικής βελτιστοποίησης
abstract: Η παρούσα διπλωματική εργασία πραγματεύεται την καθολικής βελτιστοποίησης και ειδικότερα με την ανάπτυξη και αξιολόγηση σύγχρονων μεταευρετικών αλγορίθμων για την επίλυση πολύπλοκων προβλημάτων. Αρχικά παρουσιάζονται οι βασικές έννοιες της βελτιστοποίησης, λόγου χάρη τα προβλήματα μεγιστοποίησης και ελαχιστοποίησης, τα τοπικά και ολικά ακρότατα, καθώς και οι βασικές κατηγορίες αλγορίθμων βελτιστοποίησης. Στη συνέχεια αναλύονται βελτιωμένες εκδοχές σύγχρονων μεταευρετικών μεθόδων, όπως οι: Giant-Armadillo Optimization, Optimal Foraging Algorithm, Eel and Grouper Optimizer, Differential Evolution και Magnificent Frigatebird Optimization. Για κάθε αλγόριθμο παρουσιάζονται οι προτεινόμενες τροποποιήσεις. Επιπλέον, προτείνονται νέες υβριδικές και παράλληλες προσεγγίσεις βελτιστοποίησης, με στόχο τη βελτίωση της ταχύτητας σύγκλισης και της ποιότητας των παραγόμενων λύσεων. Η αξιολόγηση των προτεινόμενων μεθόδων πραγματοποιείται μέσω πειραματικών δοκιμών σε benchmark συναρτήσεις καθολικής βελτιστοποίησης. Τα αποτελέσματα δείχνουν ότι οι προτεινόμενοι αλγόριθμοι παρουσιάζουν αυξημένη αποδοτικότητα και καλύτερη ισορροπία μεταξύ εξερεύνησης και εκμετάλλευσης σε σύγκριση με άλλες σύγχρονες μεταευρετικές τεχνικές.

title: Research on the Adaptation Algorithm of Preschool Science Education Resources Based on Federated Learning and Particle Swarm Optimisation
abstract: To address the challenges of privacy protection and data heterogeneity in adapting preschool science education resources, this paper proposes the EduSwarm-Optimised Federated Aggregation Mechanism (ESO-FAM). It is evaluated on BB-Sci2025, a de-identified dataset of 120,000 interaction records from 8,000 users over 40 virtual kindergarten nodes, in which heterogeneity is controlled by a Dirichlet concentration parameter over twelve science-topic categories, swept from α = 1.0 (near-IID) to α = 0.05 (strongly non-IID). Each node's model update is treated as a particle steered by a contribution-aware fitness function, while a proximity-gated local update separates short-lived curiosity from genuine cognitive development. Implementation uses PyTorch 2.1 with a Ray backend on four A100 GPUs, with λ = 1×10⁻⁴ and μ = 0.01. Resource-adaptation accuracy reaches 91.12%, 16.84 percentage points above FedAvg and 6.47 points above the strongest recent baseline, SCAFFOLD; convergence requires 90 rounds against 180 for FedAvg, and the communication load of 62.1 MB is 32.8% below PSO-FL. Under strong heterogeneity (α = 0.05) accuracy remains 82.5% with an average trajectory error of 0.08, whereas FedAvg falls to 42.1%. Every recommendation carries a predictive uncertainty estimate (expected calibration error 0.031), and only drift classified as substantive triggers re-aggregation. Against the four pathways reviewed here, whose accuracies remain within a 74–84% band, this work is the first to embed population-based search inside the federated aggregation step itself.

title: Infrastructure-based Monocular 3D Vehicle Localization Framework with Experimental Validation
abstract: This paper presents a one-stage learning framework that maps monocular roadside-camera images directly to vehicle states in a ground-fixed coordinate frame. Unlike conventional approaches that first detect vehicles in the image plane and subsequently apply geometric post-processing, the proposed method leverages features from a pretrained object detector to jointly estimate each vehicle's ground-plane position, dimensions, and yaw angle. The framework therefore uses visual features not only for vehicle detection but also for direct spatial and orientation estimation. To support model training and evaluation, we develop a data-collection and label-generation pipeline based on synchronized video from a roadside camera and an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Acting as a temporary top-view sensing platform, the UAV provides vehicle trajectories, dimensions, and orientations, which are transformed into the ground-fixed coordinate frame and temporally aligned with the roadside-camera images to generate ground-truth labels. The framework is evaluated using data collected during multiple experiments at the Mcity Test Facility. Results show that the proposed method can recover vehicle trajectories and orientations from monocular roadside imagery without a separate geometric post-processing stage, demonstrating its potential as a scalable approach to infrastructure-based perception at urban intersections.

title: Feed-Forward Multi-view Multi-person Reconstruction with Contrastive Human-Aware 3D Representation
abstract: Multi-view human reconstruction has been extensively studied under simplified settings, yet robust and efficient multi-person reconstruction in unconstrained environments remains challenging. Existing bottom-up methods often rely on accurate camera calibration and explicit cross-view matching, and therefore struggle with severe occlusions and ambiguities. We propose a new top-down paradigm that maintains a unified, instance-centric human-aware 3D space, enabling simultaneous camera calibration, cross-view association, and human reconstruction via cross-modal contrastive learning. Observations from multiple views are lifted and fused into this shared 3D space, where geometric structure, visual appearance, and human-centric semantic cues are jointly encoded at the instance level. We further introduce a spatial contrastive learning strategy that aligns 3D features corresponding to the same human instance across different views and modalities while separating different instances. This enables correspondence reasoning, semantic aggregation, and instance discrimination to be performed natively in 3D, improving cross-view consistency and robustness under severe occlusions. Finally, structured human body models are recovered in a feed-forward manner by regressing SMPL parameters from instance-level 3D human tokens. Extensive experiments demonstrate robust, accurate, and efficient multi-view human reconstruction in challenging real-world scenarios.

title: Embedding measure-once quantum finite automata in the Feynman quantum computer model
abstract: We present an explicit embedding of measure-once quantum finite automata (MO-QFAs) into the Feynman quantum computer model.Given an MO-QFA, we construct the corresponding Feynman machine whose register encodes both the input word and the automaton state, while a cursor evolving under a Hamiltonian implements the sequential application of the automaton transition operators.The construction relies on nested SWITCH mechanisms that select transitions according to the input symbols.We prove that, for every MO-QFA and every input word, measuring the cursor in its final position yields exactly the quantum state reached by the automaton after processing the same input.Consequently, acceptance probabilities are preserved exactly, and every language recognized by an MO-QFA with cutpoint can be recognized within the Feynman framework with the same acceptance behavior.This establishes an explicit connection between discrete-time quantum computation and continuous-time, physically motivated Hamiltonian models.

abstract: Tantangan utama dalam pengembangan chatbot medis adalah ketidakmampuan sistem memahami istilah teknis yang kompleks dan variasi bahasa pengguna yang tidak baku. Pendekatan pemrosesan berbasis kata (word-level) sering gagal menangkap makna morfologis istilah medis, menyebabkan tingginya angka Unknown Intent. Penelitian ini bertujuan meningkatkan ketepatan pemrosesan pertanyaan pada dataset AI Medical Chatbot dengan mengintegrasikan metode tokenisasi Byte-Pair Encoding (BPE) dan klasifikasi Support Vector Machine (SVM), serta menerapkan strategi Semi-Supervised Learning melalui Pseudo-Labeling untuk menangani data tidak berlabel. Penelitian dilakukan dengan metodologi CRISP-DM, membandingkan model Baseline (TF-IDF), model BPE Teroptimasi, dan model BPE dengan Pseudo-Labeling. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan bahwa tokenisasi BPE mampu mengatasi masalah Out-of-Vocabulary (OOV) dengan baik. Model BPE dengan Hyperparameter Tuning mencapai akurasi 93,86%, mengungguli model Baseline yang tertahan di angka 90,89% pada dataset kompleks. Selanjutnya, penerapan strategi Full Coverage Pseudo-Labeling (Model V2) terbukti menjadi konfigurasi paling optimal. Meskipun mengalami sedikit koreksi akurasi menjadi 93,65%, model ini berhasil mengonversi 100% data unknown menjadi pengetahuan latih yang berguna, menghilangkan blind spot sistem tanpa mengorbankan presisi secara drastis. Sistem akhir diimplementasikan dengan fitur Language Guardrail hybrid yang mampu menangani input medis pendek secara responsif. Penelitian ini menyimpulkan bahwa tokenisasi subkata dan pemanfaatan data unreliable secara menyeluruh adalah kunci untuk membangun chatbot medis yang tangguh. Kata kunci: Byte-Pair Encoding, Support Vector Machine, chatbot medis, klasifikasi intent, pemrosesan bahasa alami.

title: AGCP — Artificial Genome-Coded Plasticity
abstract: AGCP studies whether non-linear cognition can emerge in evolutionary artificial organisms whose sparse spiking neural networks are grown from a generative genome and adapted online by inference-time plasticity. Inheritance is strictly Darwinian: organisms inherit the generator, never lifetime-trained weights.

title: Método Reprodutível para Avaliar a Resiliência de Agentes LLM a Ataques de Injeção Indireta de Prompt
abstract: Com agentes LLM operando sobre conteúdo não confiável, a injeção indireta de prompt (IPI) sustenta riscos agênticos como o Agent Goal Hijack. Este artigo propõe um método reprodutível de ataque por IPI: instrumento de avaliação de resiliência com desenho adaptativo in-the-loop, oráculo canary, invariantes e experimento estatístico (N=30 por célula; 900 ensaios) com três defensores sob condições idênticas. As taxas foram 0% para o Opus 4.8 (0/300; IC Wilson 99% ≤2,2%), 42,0% para o Haiku 4.5 e 61,7% para o Sonnet 4.5, todas as diferenças significativas; ressalvado que atacante e defensor mais resistente são o mesmo modelo (Opus 4.8). No desenho avaliado, o vazamento exigiu receita funcional de localização; o Sonnet vazou mais que o Haiku.

title: Capability-based checked exceptions for Cangjie: a compiler prototype
abstract: An implementation, in the real Cangjie compiler and standard library, of capability-based checked exceptions: throwing a checked exception of type E requires a capability of type CanThrow , produced only by a try-catch handling E and carried down the call stack as an implicit, compile-time-erased parameter declared by a throws clause. Capabilities are inferred where the declaration allows it and vanish entirely after type checking, so the discipline costs nothing at run time, changes no ABI, and puts no effect polymorphism in user signatures. The same mechanism checks effect-handler requirements through a performs clause and CanPerform. The deposit contains the design document the implementation follows, the engineering record (architecture, the rulings and decisions taken, the running proposal-vs-implementation gap ledger, the test baseline), the containerised build and test driver, and the complete delta of the work as git format-patch series against the upstream Cangjie repositories: 97 patches over four repositories, 303 files, roughly 9,700 inserted lines, together with the upstream commit each series applies to. What the archive does not contain. The four modified repositories are referenced as git submodules, and a source archive carries no submodule content. The code itself is therefore reached either through the repositories listed under related identifiers, or by reconstructing it from upstream with the included patch series, for which patches/README.md gives the commands. State of the work. The checking pipeline is built end to end - clauses, elaboration, capability-aware subtyping and override checking, the demand/supply pass, inference, cross-package metadata, migration annotations for the standard library - and is gated by a suite of 164 test files of its own, green alongside the compiler's full semantic, incremental-compilation and macro suites. One soundness item is known-open and identified in the record: an inferred capability list does not reach the expression type, so a function value formed inside a discharging try, stored outward and called after it, is accepted and throws uncaught. Escape analysis of every kind is out of scope by design ruling; it belongs to the parallel Modal Cangjie proposal. The guarantee delivered here is complete demand/supply checking plus machine-verified documentation of what each declaration may throw, not the full lifetime guarantee.

title: Charming Thicket Rat: A Metaheuristic Algorithm Inspired by the Foraging Behavior of the Thicket Rat
abstract: This paper introduces a novel metaheuristic algorithm, "Charming Thicket Rat" (CTR), inspired by the foraging behavior of the thicket rat ( *Neotoma benjaminii*). Thicket rats are known for their intricate and seemingly random movement patterns within dense thickets, navigating complex terrain while efficiently searching for food. CTR leverages this observed behavior to develop a new optimization strategy. The algorithm utilizes a "thicket" representation to model the search space, simulating the rat's movement through a complex environment. A "charm" mechanism, mimicking the rat's selective attraction to promising food sources, biases the search towards more promising solutions. We present the algorithm's design, including key parameters and their influence on performance. Empirical evaluations on a range of benchmark optimization problems demonstrate that CTR exhibits competitive performance compared to established metaheuristic algorithms, particularly in challenging, high-dimensional search spaces. The algorithm's effectiveness stems from its ability to escape local optima and maintain a diverse population of solutions, guided by the inherent exploration and exploitation strategies embedded within its design. Further research will focus on refining the "charm" mechanism and exploring its applicability to various real-world optimization problems.

title: Messages Passed Along the Edges: A Contemporary Synthesis Review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data
abstract: This article presents a narrative review of Graph Neural Networks for Relational Data in the context of Artificial Intelligence. The literature on this topic has expanded substantially over recent decades, yet it remains fragmented across subfields, methods, and national research traditions. Drawing on an interpretive synthesis of representative contributions, the review reconstructs the historical development of the area, examines the conceptual foundations and definitional disputes that organize its debates, and maps the contemporary landscape of research, including the methodological shift toward data-intensive approaches and the institutional pressures that shape publication practice. Particular attention is given to the role of GNN and graph learning as organizing themes, and to the conditions under which findings from different research traditions can be brought into productive comparison. The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Cape Dune Molerat Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CDMOA)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel metaheuristic optimization algorithm, the Cape Dune Molerat Metaheuristic Optimization Algorithm (CDMOA), inspired by the foraging behavior of Cape Dune Molesrats (Xenoprotomys capeensis) in the Namib Desert. The algorithm leverages the molerat's unique strategy of traversing sand dunes, utilizing both forward and backward movements, and adapting its path based on perceived slope and terrain. CDMOA employs a population-based search strategy with a novel representation of the solution space based on dune coordinates and a dynamic adjustment of movement probabilities influenced by a simulated "slope gradient" and "terrain complexity" metric. The algorithm incorporates a self-adaptation mechanism for its parameters, aiming to improve convergence speed and exploration capabilities. The performance of CDMOA is evaluated across a range of benchmark optimization problems, demonstrating competitive results against established metaheuristic algorithms such as the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). The core of CDMOA lies in its ability to efficiently navigate complex search landscapes by strategically combining exploration and exploitation phases, mimicking the molerat's natural adaptation to its environment. The algorithm's parameters are tuned through a simulated annealing process to further enhance its performance. Finally, the paper concludes with a discussion of the algorithm's strengths, limitations, and potential future research directions.

title: Microscopic Quantum Control: An Adaptive Algorithm
abstract: This paper presents a novel self-adaptive quantum control algorithm designed to dynamically adjust the properties of quantum bits in response to environmental changes. The algorithm leverages the principles of quantum entanglement and self-adaptation to achieve robust and versatile control. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through a series of simulations and analyses, showcasing its ability to maintain coherence and control over quantum states across a range of perturbations. The core mechanism centers around the strategic application of entanglement and the adaptive calculation of quantum states, resulting in a significantly enhanced control capability compared to existing techniques. This work offers a promising pathway towards scalable and adaptable quantum control systems.

title: Dynamic Topology for Quantum Entanglement Correction
abstract: Quantum entanglement is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, holding immense potential for secure communication and advanced computation. However, entanglement is notoriously fragile, susceptible to decoherence and disturbance. Quantum error correction is crucial to maintaining entanglement, but current error correction techniques often rely on computationally intensive and limited methods. This paper introduces a novel quantum entanglement correction algorithm based on dynamic topology, designed to enhance the efficiency and accuracy of error correction through a dynamically adjusted state. The core mechanism leverages the inherent topological properties of quantum states to actively compensate for environmental noise, ultimately improving the robustness of quantum systems. We demonstrate the effectiveness of this approach through theoretical analysis and preliminary experimental validation, showcasing a significant improvement in error correction performance compared to existing methods.

title: Dynamic Topology Neural Networks (DTNNs) Learning
abstract: This paper introduces Dynamic Topology Neural Networks (DTNNs), a novel approach to neural network design that leverages continuous topological evolution and feedback learning to autonomously construct and optimize network topologies. Unlike traditional static neural networks, DTNNs adapt their structure in real-time, responding to evolving input data and task requirements. The core mechanism involves a graph-based neural network framework where neurons and connections form a dynamic topology. Each neuron possesses a state vector, influencing its activation level, connection weights, and local environmental information. Topological evolution is governed by mechanisms, such as genetic algorithms or reinforcement learning, dynamically adjusting the network's structure by adding, removing, or modifying connections based on neuron states and network performance metrics. Simultaneously, feedback learning updates neuron activation levels through gradient descent or pulse feedback, driven by input signals and performance objectives. This architecture offers enhanced adaptability, robustness, and scalability, surpassing the limitations of static networks in handling unstructured and dynamic data. The key innovation lies in the dynamic control of topology and the deep learning of neuron states, providing a more flexible and powerful framework for complex data processing.

title: 多体量子纠缠的拓扑分析
abstract: This paper explores the application of a novel approach to the analysis of quantum entanglement, specifically focusing on its implications for the development of efficient quantum communication. We propose a framework leveraging the unique properties of multi-particle quantum entanglement to unveil the underlying topological structure within complex quantum systems. Our core mechanism centers around the manipulation of entanglement to induce topological phases, ultimately enhancing the fidelity and speed of quantum information transfer. This work contributes to a deeper understanding of quantum entanglement and its potential for revolutionizing quantum communication protocols.

The review identifies three synthetic conclusions: the literature is cumulatively strong but organizationally weak; methodological pluralism is better understood as a resource than as a defect; and the growing practical salience of the topic raises the stakes of its unresolved conceptual questions. An agenda for future work is proposed, emphasizing integrative research designs, transparent synthesis practices, and the protection of definitional and infrastructural work on which cumulative progress depends. The article is intended as both a reference map for newcomers and a provocation for specialists in Artificial Intelligence.

title: Neuro-Symbolic Integration of Graph Attention Networks and Knowledge Graphs for Interpretable Personality Prediction from Digital Footprints
abstract: Abstract This paper addresses the problem of interpretable personality prediction from social media digital footprints. While modern deep learning models demonstrate high accuracy in personality assessment tasks, their black-box nature limits their applicability in psychologically and socially sensitive domains. To overcome this limitation, a neuro-symbolic approach is proposed that combines neural feature extraction from textual and visual data with reasoning over a domain-specific knowledge graph. The architecture integrates Graph Attention Networks to model relationships between observable digital behaviors and personality traits defined by Cattell’s 16 Personality Factors. The study evaluates the proposed approach on social media profiles with psychometric annotations and demonstrates that the model provides competitive predictive performance while enabling transparent and psychologically meaningful explanations.

title: Exploring acoustic features and predictive modeling for automatic fluency assessment in Korean as a foreign language*
abstract: Research on fluency assessment in Korean as a foreign language (KFL) has primarily focused on assessment constructs and manual scoring, whereas studies on automatic fluency assessment remain limited. This study aims to explore effective fluency features for automatic fluency assessment of KFL learners and to compare the performance of different predictive models based on these features. Temporal (T5), acoustic (A8 and A88), and hybrid (H13 and H93) feature sets combining temporal and acoustic features were constructed and applied to tree-based models [Gradient Boosting Classifier (GBC) and XGBoost (XGB)] and transformer-based models for tabular data [FT-Transformer (FTT) and SAINT]. Experiments were conducted on 1,672,398 training and 209,083 validation utterances from the AIHub Korean Learner Speech Corpus. To examine the effect of data imbalance, performance was evaluated under original and balanced score-distribution conditions. Quadratic weighted kappa was the primary metric. Accuracy, Pearson’s correlation coefficient (r), root mean squared error, and Macro-F1 were supplementary metrics. Under original conditions, each model's acoustic condition outperformed its temporal and hybrid conditions. A8 was highest for GBC and XGB, A88 for FTT and SAINT, and SAINT-A88 overall. Hybrid sets showed no consistent improvements. Under balanced conditions, patterns varied, but SAINT-A88 remained the best-performing configuration. These findings indicate that performance varied across the feature conditions and predictive models examined.

title: Large Language Models and Prompt Engineering
abstract: This book provides a structured and accessible introduction to the theory, design, and real-world use of large language models (LLMs). As generative AI systems become embedded across industries, this book offers readers a balanced perspective that combines technical foundations with practical guidance and critical reflection. Beginning with the fundamentals of LLMs and prompt engineering, this book progressively explores advanced prompting techniques, application and interaction frameworks, and the underlying architectures that power modern language models. Dedicated chapters examine how LLMs are being applied in high-impact domains such as healthcare, customer support, and education, highlighting design principles, implementation considerations, and illustrative case studies. The book also addresses model fine-tuning, evaluation methods, and the ethical, social, and regulatory challenges associated with deploying LLMs at scale. This book supports readers in: · Understanding prompt engineering strategies and application frameworks · Gaining insight into contemporary LLM architecture and capabilities · Designing and evaluating LLM-based systems across real-world domains · Considering ethics, safety, and human-centered aspects of LLM deployment This book is a practical, accessible resource for those seeking to work thoughtfully and responsibly with LLMs in both academic and applied settings.

title: Adaptive error type detection algorithm for English learner corpora using reinforcement learning integration
abstract: Abstract Error type detection in English learner corpora faces significant challenges due to the long-tailed distribution of error categories, where conventional supervised methods exhibit degraded performance on underrepresented but pedagogically important error types. This study proposes an adaptive error type detection algorithm that integrates reinforcement learning with dynamic reward mechanisms, formulating the detection task as a Markov Decision Process wherein an agent assigns error type labels based on state representations incorporating contextualized BERT encodings, attention-weighted historical predictions, and global sentence features, while an adaptive reward mechanism dynamically adjusts category weights based on frequency distribution and real-time detection performance. Experimental evaluation on the FCE and BEA 2019 benchmark corpora demonstrates that the proposed method achieves Micro-F0.5 scores of 63.9% and 66.4% with Macro-F0.5 scores of 51.2% and 52.8%, representing 4.1 and 3.7 percentage point improvements over GECToR and 1.8 and 1.7 percentage point improvements over the strongest reweighted supervised baseline (BERT + Class-balanced loss) on the class-balanced metric, while reducing frequency-performance correlation from r = 0.76 to r = 0.58 and achieving 22.6% relative improvement on low-frequency error categories. The proposed framework effectively addresses class imbalance challenges in error type detection, providing methodological insights for long-tailed classification problems and demonstrating practical potential for intelligent language learning systems requiring accurate and fine-grained error feedback across diverse grammatical categories.

title: Architecting Conversational Data Systems for Stateless LLM APIs: The Hydration Proxy Pattern
abstract: As enterprise platforms transition to conversational reasoning interfaces, the stateless nature of LLM APIs creates an architectural gap. While statelessness enables horizontal scalability for AI providers, it forces client applications to manage the entire burden of conversational state and semantic memory. The work identifies the Hydration Proxy Pattern, an architecture that decouples session persistence from the reasoning engine. The framework ensures platform sovereignty over conversational data while enabling secure, multi-stage semantic grounding. We further propose the Context Stabilization Mandate to resolve the tradeoff between sovereign state management and KV caching.

title: Predicting Phase Ordering in Chaotic Maps and Coupled Map Lattices
abstract: Coupled logistic maps exhibit collective ordering of their directional phases. As the system parameter varies, the directional phases can undergo a transition from an in-phase state to an anti-phase state, while the individual map trajectories remain chaotic. In this work, we propose a data-driven machine learning (ML) framework based on parameter-aware reservoir computing (PARC) to predict order-parameter dynamics in two representative systems: a logistic map and a two-dimensional coupled map lattice (CML). For the logistic map, the reservoir is trained using only pre-crisis time series data at bifurcation parameter $μ$ values below the attractor-merging crisis ($μ_0 = 3.6786$). The trained reservoir reconstructs the full bifurcation diagram and correctly predicts the transition in the directional order parameter $M(μ)$, from an ordered state ($M \approx 0$) to a disordered state ($M \neq 0$) across the crisis point. For the CML, we exploit the spatial homogeneity of the lattice: a single reservoir is trained on the dynamics of one representative lattice site and is then replicated across all $L^2$ sites during prediction, where $L$=50. The replicated reservoir correctly predicts the transition from in-phase synchronization ($θ\approx 1$) to anti-phase clustered states ($θ\approx 0$) at $μ\approx 3.82$, where $θ$ quantifies phase coherence across lattice sites.

title: Mind the Rift: Cross-Scale Coupling Mismatch for AI-Generated Video Detection
abstract: As AI video generators achieve cinematic realism, reliable detection becomes essential for safeguarding digital trust. We identify cross-scale coupling mismatch as a new forensic signal, where scale refers to the level of abstraction (semantic dynamics vs. pixel-level residuals): in natural videos, macro-level temporal dynamics and micro-level residual patterns are intrinsically coupled by the unified imaging physics pipeline, whereas AI generators, whose training objectives do not explicitly preserve this joint distribution, systematically violate this coupling. Detecting such mismatch is challenging because it requires independently extracting information at both scales while simultaneously quantifying their cross-scale relationship. We propose RIFT (Representation Inconsistency Forensics on Trajectories), an orthogonal forensic framework that addresses this through three interlocking components: a macro stream that builds a dynamic baseline of expected temporal evolution via differential geometry and persistent homology on learned manifold trajectories, a micro stream that acts as a sensitive forensic probe via steganalytic filtering and temporal modeling, and a coupling divergence module that measures the conditional dependency between the two streams. Gram-Schmidt orthogonality guarantees the information-theoretic validity of this measurement. Experiments on two benchmarks (VidProM, 120K videos, 7 generators; GenVidBench, 68K videos, 4 generators) demonstrate that RIFT achieves 99.33% and 99.72% F1-score respectively, with 97.87% unseen-generator detection rate in leave-one-out evaluation, while exhibiting encoder agnosticism: scaling from ViT-S/14 (22M) to ViT-L/14 (300M) changes F1 by less than 0.1%, and switching to a different encoder family (DINOv1) reduces F1 by only 0.73 pp. Code is available at https://github.com/Litsay/RIFT

title: 自己教師あり学習に基づく事前学習モデルの下流タスクとしてのマルチインスタンス学習
abstract: Multi-instance learning (MIL) is a type of weakly supervised learning. In MIL, a set of instances is defined as a bag, and only bag labels are known. In recent years, deep learning-based MIL has been applied in medical imaging, especially in histopathological images. However, when classifying the marker in the brain hematoma CT images which we deal with, simply applying MIL leads to spurious correlations. In addition, many studies applying MIL to histopathological images handle thousands of instances per bag and show high performance, while our task struggles to learn with a few hundred instances per bag and has low performance. In this paper, we address these problems. We propose using a pre-trained model with self-supervised learning for the multi-instance learner as a downstream task. We apply self-supervised learning to the instance feature extractor in MIL to learn effective feature representations of patch images. The experimental results demonstrate that our method achieves improvements of 6.5% in accuracy and11.2% in the F1-score without falling into the spurious correlation problem.

title: Human-Centered Evaluation Measures of Explainable AI for Clinical Decision Support: A Scoping Review
abstract: The black box nature of machine learning (ML) models presents substantial challenges for clinical decision support systems (CDSS), limiting trust and adoption by clinicians. Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) aims to address this by enhancing transparency and interpretability in clinical settings. This scoping review focuses on how explainability is evaluated in clinician-facing CDSS, synthesizing human-centered evaluation metrics and measurement approaches rather than technical methods.

title: AGENTIC LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS: A SYSTEMATIC REVIEW OF ARCHITECTURES, REASONING, AND MULTI-AGENT COLLABORATION
abstract: Agentic large language models (LLMs)-systems that couple a foundation model with an execution loop for perception, planning, memory, tool use, and multi-step action-have moved from research prototypes to widely deployed infrastructure since 2022.This review synthesizes the 2023-2026 literature on agentic LLMs across four dimensions: architectures (single-and multi-agent, monolithic and modular), reasoning and planning (chain-of-thought, ReAct, Tree-of-Thoughts, and reflection-based self-correction), tool use (function calling, retrieval, and post-execution verification), and multi-agent collaboration (centralized, decentralized, and hierarchical coordination).Using a review protocol modeled on PRISMA guidance, we screened literature from arXiv, ACL/ICLR/NeurIPS proceedings, and primary industry technical reports, applying explicit inclusion and exclusion criteria and developing a structured taxonomy through iterative coding of fifty primary sources.We synthesize empirical evidence on when multi-agent systems outperform single agents-and when they do not: large-scale failure analyses find that coordination and verification failures, rather than base-model capability alone, account for the majority of multi-agent task failures.We map the benchmark landscape (GAIA, SWEbench, WebArena, AgentBench) and emerging "time-horizon" metrics that track rapid, measurable growth in the length of tasks agents can complete autonomously.We then examine open challenges in reliability, safety, and governance before turning to the technical and policy levers-compute, full-stack export strategy, standards leadership, and talent-most relevant to sustaining U.S. leadership in agentic artificial intelligence amid intensifying international competition.We close with a forward-looking research agenda spanning verifiable evaluation, self-improving systems, and multi-agent security.

title: Defesa Distribuída: Avaliação do Aprendizado Federado para Detecção de Ataques em Sistemas Operacionais
abstract: A detecção dinâmica de aplicações móveis maliciosas requer rastros de execução amplos, recentes e representativos. Como a maioria das abordagens utiliza técnicas de aprendizado de máquina para essa detecção, há demanda por centralizar grandes volumes de dados para o treinamento dos modelos. Porém, essa centralização é dificultada por diversos desafios. A coleta de sequências de chamadas de sistema requer instrumentação custosa das aplicações, as diferenças entre dispositivos e versões do sistema geram distribuições heterogêneas de dados, e a concentração de dados compromete a privacidade e consome recursos críticos em dispositivos móveis e de borda. Assim, este trabalho propõe um mecanismo de detecção distribuído baseado em Aprendizado Federado, que permite treinar modelos localmente e compartilhar apenas suas atualizações com um servidor de agregação. O método alcança 0,900 de acurácia, 0,896 de F1-macro e 0,922 de AUPRC, além de reduzir significativamente o tráfego de dados em comparação com abordagens centralizadas, conciliando a efetividade das abordagens de aprendizado de máquina com as restrições de privacidade e recursos dos dispositivos.

title: Title: Fractal Self-Similarity for Algorithmic Complexity Analysis
abstract: This paper explores the application of fractal self-similarity to the analysis of algorithmic complexity. Traditional complexity measures, while valuable, often overlook the underlying structural properties of algorithms, leading to incomplete understanding of computational resource utilization. We propose a novel metric, based on the self-similarity of the algorithm's output, to quantify this structure and identify computationally expensive regions. This framework aims to provide a more precise and insightful assessment of algorithm complexity, potentially guiding algorithm design and resource allocation. The study begins with a formal definition of the self-similarity metric and demonstrates its potential for quantifying computational resource demands across various algorithms. The paper concludes with a discussion of the implications of this approach for both theoretical and practical applications.

title: ## Cape Horseshoe Bat-Inspired Metaheuristic Algorithm for Complex Optimization Problems
abstract: This paper presents a novel metaheuristic algorithm, termed the "Cape Horseshoe Bat Algorithm" (CHBA), inspired by the unique echolocation and navigation strategies of the Cape Horseshoe Bat (Hipposideros abyssinus). The bat's ability to detect prey and navigate in complex environments through sophisticated sound emission and analysis has motivated the development of an optimization approach that leverages similar principles. The CHBA algorithm utilizes a combination of position encoding, adaptive parameter control, and a novel convergence criterion based on echo-simulated distance. The algorithm aims to effectively explore the search space and converge to optimal or near-optimal solutions for complex optimization problems. The core mechanism involves simulating the bat's echolocation process to dynamically adjust the algorithm's parameters and guide the search towards promising regions. The performance of the CHBA algorithm is evaluated on a range of benchmark functions, demonstrating its competitive capabilities compared to established metaheuristic algorithms. The algorithm's design emphasizes robustness, adaptability, and efficiency, making it a viable option for tackling various real-world optimization challenges. The key innovation lies in the application of echolocation principles to parameter adaptation and convergence assessment, providing a unique perspective on metaheuristic design.

title: Quantum Entanglement Information Weaving Algorithm
abstract: Quantum entanglement, a fundamental phenomenon in quantum mechanics, offers a unique pathway to enhanced computational capabilities. This paper investigates the potential of utilizing quantum entanglement to revolutionize information processing, specifically through the development of a novel algorithm dubbed "Quantum Entanglement Information Weaving" (QEIA). We explore a new computational paradigm predicated on leveraging entanglement to achieve higher precision and efficiency in quantum computation, and propose a distributed quantum information network architecture built upon this principle. The core mechanism centers around designing a quantum algorithm that harnesses entanglement to facilitate parallel processing and optimized data transfer, ultimately enabling collaborative quantum computation. This research aims to establish a foundational basis for future quantum computing advancements, particularly through the application of entanglement-based techniques.

title: 基于自适应的概率逻辑推理引擎
abstract: This paper introduces a novel probabilistic logic reasoning engine based on adaptive strategies. Traditional approaches often rely on predefined rules, struggling with complex and uncertain problems. This work proposes a mechanism that dynamically adjusts reasoning strategies based on historical results, significantly enhancing inference efficiency. The core of the system involves a self-learning inference policy, allowing the engine to adapt to the specific characteristics of each problem. We explore a framework for implementing this adaptive approach, focusing on optimizing the learning process and evaluating its performance on benchmark datasets. The paper concludes with a discussion of the potential benefits and limitations of this approach, highlighting its promise for tackling a wider range of challenging problems.

title: 基于概率逻辑的复杂度分析与优化
abstract: This paper investigates the application of probabilistic logic to complexity analysis and optimization within the context of algorithm design. The core aim is to establish a novel framework for evaluating algorithm complexity by leveraging probabilistic distributions, and to propose a probabilistic logic optimization algorithm designed to minimize computational cost. The proposed method aims to move beyond static complexity assessments by incorporating dynamic assessment through probabilistic models. This research explores how probability distributions can be used to represent algorithm behavior and how these distributions can be refined through optimization algorithms to achieve enhanced efficiency. The paper presents a mechanism for evaluating algorithm complexity using probabilistic models and a novel optimization algorithm based on probability distributions to reduce computational burden. The focus is on providing a practical approach to improve algorithm performance through intelligent computational resource management.
